raw_title: Chevy Reportedly Axes Plans for the Corvette SUV and EV
title: Chevy Reportedly Axes Plans for the Corvette SUV and EV
raw_summary: The imagined future of a broad lineup of Corvette-badged SUVs, sedans, and electric vehicles that some of us dreamed about—or perhaps dreaded—is no longer set to become a reality. GM’s long-rumored plans to build out the Corvette brand as a broader lineup have been shelved, according to a report by GM Authority citing sources within the company. We’ve been discussing the possibility of a Corvette SUV for years now, and this Porsche Cayenne –fighting model appears to be the most significant casualty of this news. Electric power had also been discussed for a future Corvette, and Chevrolet does currently offer two hybrid powertrains in the C8 Corvette, but it now sounds like GM’s upcoming electric-vehicle platforms won’t be making their way into any models with a Corvette badge. The report even mentions rumors of a four-door Corvette sedan that now isn’t likely to ever see the light of day.

Electric power had also been discussed for a future Corvette, and Chevrolet does currently offer two hybrid powertrains in the C8 Corvette, but it now sounds like GM’s upcoming electric-vehicle platforms won’t be making their way into any models with a Corvette badge. The report even mentions rumors of a four-door Corvette sedan that now isn’t likely to ever see the light of day.

This potential Corvette spin-off series could have been a cash cow for GM, much like how the large sales volumes and profits of Porsche’s SUV models help fund its sports-car development. But perhaps GM’s decision hinges on the softer demand for EVs lately, or the backlash it anticipated from Corvette loyalists who might think that offering a Corvette-badged SUV sullies the iconic name. Because GM had never officially announced these plans to begin with, it’s all a bit murky, and Chevrolet representatives said they had nothing to add to this speculation when Car and Driver reached out for comment.

raw_title: Driving A 43-Horsepower Geo Metro Convertible From New York To Los Angeles Looks Really Miserable
title: Driving A 43-Horsepower Geo Metro Convertible From New York To Los Angeles Looks Really Miserable
raw_summary: The Geo Metro Convertible is one of the silliest cars ever sold in America. The Metro hatchback was already a misfit on American roads, with its microscopic 1.0-liter three-cylinder engine, 1,600-pound curb weight, and $7,000-ish starting price. It was a General Motors rebadge of a Suzuki Swift, and it almost immediately became the butt of every automotive joke. There was no logical reason, then, for any engineer to lop off its roof and turn it into a convertible, but that didn't stop it from happening, and honestly I'm grateful GM sold them anyway. I doubt GM ever imagined that a YouTuber would end up driving one from New York to Los Angeles 34 years after it was built, but that's just what Mitchell Kohrmann did in his latest video . When new, the Geo Metro convertible was fabled to have 55 horsepower and 58 pound-feet of torque, but Kohrmann was smart enough to dyno test his remarkably clean 1992 Metro convertible before setting off on his cross-continental journey. Before that, though, he gave it a tune-up and fixed the air conditioning — or at least he thought he did... After a 50-second pull, the dyno showed the Metro made 43 horsepower and 53 lb-ft of torque. That's more than enough to complete a 2,838-mile road trip that includes a 10,000-foot climb, right?

article_paragraphs: The Geo Metro Convertible is one of the silliest cars ever sold in America. The Metro hatchback was already a misfit on American roads, with its microscopic 1.0-liter three-cylinder engine, 1,600-pound curb weight, and $7,000-ish starting price. It was a General Motors rebadge of a Suzuki Swift, and it almost immediately became the butt of every automotive joke. There was no logical reason, then, for any engineer to lop off its roof and turn it into a convertible, but that didn't stop it from happening, and honestly I'm grateful GM sold them anyway. I doubt GM ever imagined that a YouTuber would end up driving one from New York to Los Angeles 34 years after it was built, but that's just what Mitchell Kohrmann did in his latest video .

When new, the Geo Metro convertible was fabled to have 55 horsepower and 58 pound-feet of torque, but Kohrmann was smart enough to dyno test his remarkably clean 1992 Metro convertible before setting off on his cross-continental journey. Before that, though, he gave it a tune-up and fixed the air conditioning — or at least he thought he did... After a 50-second pull, the dyno showed the Metro made 43 horsepower and 53 lb-ft of torque. That's more than enough to complete a 2,838-mile road trip that includes a 10,000-foot climb, right?

I had never seen any of Kohrmann's videos before watching this one, but looking at his other uploads, he's no stranger to long drives, including a 10,050-mile drive to the Arctic Ocean in a Touareg V10 diesel , and a 6,500-mile drive in a V10 Audi S8. Those are both leather-lined luxury cruisers, though, and going from that to a vinyl-topped three-cylinder economy car must feel like quite the downgrade. With just 43 horsepower, Kohrmann ends up keeping the little Metro's gas pedal in contact with the floor a lot more than I expected.

The calamities begin before he even starts his journey, since he realized the Geo's tires may have looked fine at first, but they were utterly ancient, so he had to source some 155/80R13 tires at the last minute. Fortunately he finds some that will fit, and sets off on the drive. Predictably, the drive into and out of Manhattan involves navigating excruciating traffic jams, but once he gets out away from New York, he starts covering more ground.

This video is about 1.5 hours long, and includes lots of POV shots as well as breakdown and repair content and tons of beautiful scenery. Kohrmann initially intended to attempt to beat some sub-1.0-liter engine Cannonball Run record of 48 hours, 9 minutes and 53 seconds that was set in 1964 by a Sunbeam Imp, but he gives up on that after a series of setbacks. Regardless, he still completes the journey in 49 hours, 11 minutes and 18 seconds, after a harrowing journey filled with twists, turns, breakdowns, and hellish traffic jams. I think it's worth a watch. Cheers to you, Mitchell, for following through on what looks like an utterly miserable journey, but a really cool video.

article_paragraphs: Toyota is giving its best-selling Corolla a major makeover, and an all-electric version is part of the plan. The upcoming Corolla Cross EV was captured in public for the first time ahead of its expected 2027 debut.
The Corolla has always been “a car for everyone,” Toyota’s former president and current CEO, Koji Sato, said after unveiling the next-gen Corolla Concept at last year’s Japan Mobility Show.
Since it went on sale 60 years ago, over 57 million drivers have chosen the Corolla, making it Toyota’s best-selling vehicle ever.
The Corolla has undergone 12 model changes since 1966, but the compact car is about to undergo its biggest transformation yet.
Although it’s still a top seller, the Corolla has lost some of its appeal as new, more advanced, and efficient options have emerged. Toyota looks to change that with the next-generation model.
It will remain “a car for everyone,” as Sato said, but the next-gen Corolla will come in multiple powertrains, including an all-electric version.

“Whether it’s a battery EV, plug-in hybrid, hybrid, or internal combustion engine vehicle―whatever the power source―let’s make good-looking cars that everyone will want to drive,” Sato said at the Japan Mobility Show last October.
Ahead of its expected debut sometime in 2027, a disguised Corolla Cross EV was spotted driving near Toyota’s European headquarters and R&D center.

title: Everything we learned from F1's 2026 Mexican Grand Prix
raw_summary: Formula 1’s new champion was crowned amid an action-packed Mexican Grand Prix weekend that taught us plenty. It's now a pattern of behaviour, and this time it cost Ferrari a very likely win and a probable 1-2. Charles Leclerc's attack on Lewis Hamilton on lap one and Hamilton's response to it opened a door through which Max Verstappen happily walked. But it should never have been open at all had Ferrari had a robust team tactics plan in place - or, much more importantly given what unfolded, any hope of trusting its drivers to smoothly execute it.

Charles Leclerc's attack on Lewis Hamilton on lap one and Hamilton's response to it opened a door through which Max Verstappen happily walked.
article_paragraphs: Formula 1’s new champion was crowned amid an action-packed Mexican Grand Prix weekend that taught us plenty.

It's now a pattern of behaviour, and this time it cost Ferrari a very likely win and a probable 1-2. Charles Leclerc's attack on Lewis Hamilton on lap one and Hamilton's response to it opened a door through which Max Verstappen happily walked. But it should never have been open at all had Ferrari had a robust team tactics plan in place - or, much more importantly given what unfolded, any hope of trusting its drivers to smoothly execute it.

That lack of trust was the main takeaway from just how the Ferrari situation kept unspooling as Sunday night progressed in Mexico. Every new interview Fred Vasseur did sounded more exasperated. Hamilton's condemnation of Leclerc's approach to intra-team racing in general got more blunt as the post-race press conference went on.
"I think it's a mentality thing. It's like 'do or die - either I win or none of us do', and it shouldn't be that. It should be us getting that 1-2," was Hamilton's most damning line.

But it had also been Hamilton calling for the stewards to penalise Leclerc in the race at a point where Red Bull would have been the direct beneficiary. And they'd both outbraked themselves while fixated on beating each other on lap one. Meanwhile, Leclerc just tried to redirect any angst towards the circuit layout (how careless of the organisers not to barrier-line the track so he couldn't corner cut to overtake his team-mate) and suggest the intra-team element didn't really seem much of a "talking point".

This is a mess. It can be plastered over with some talks or new guidelines. But fundamentally these are two drivers who don't trust each other to have the team's best interests at heart, and who are giving their team little reason to trust them. - Matt Beer
F1 can feel quite fortunate that Leclerc didn’t win the race because he cut the track to gain the race lead.

Thankfully for F1, Verstappen was able to stay just within five seconds of Leclerc and Red Bull cleverly pitted him immediately when Leclerc served his penalty to ensure Verstappen got track position.

raw_title: Why Antonelli's rejecting #1 for 2027 F1 season
title: Why Antonelli's rejecting #1 for 2027 F1 season
raw_summary: Formula 1 world champion Kimi Antonelli has explained why he is choosing not to run with the title winner's #1 on his car next season. The Italian made history at the Mexican Grand Prix as he became the youngest driver to ever win the crown at the age of 20.
summary: Formula 1 world champion Kimi Antonelli has explained why he is choosing not to run with the title winner's #1 on his car next season. The Italian made history at the Mexican Grand Prix as he became the youngest driver to ever win the crown at the age of 20.
article_paragraphs: Formula 1 world champion Kimi Antonelli has explained why he is choosing not to run with the title winner's #1 on his car next season.
The Italian made history at the Mexican Grand Prix as he became the youngest driver to ever win the crown at the age of 20.
That feat gives him the opportunity if he chooses to run with the #1 on his car next season, as 2025 champion Lando Norris has done this season.
However, Antonelli has said that he will stick with his current #12 - as that number has personal significance for him, plus he has not had the best of luck in the past when he has run with #1.
Antonelli chose #12 as his F1 race number to honour his hero Ayrton Senna, who raced with it during his Lotus years from 1985-87 as well as in his first title-winning campaign with McLaren in 1988.

Asked whether he would take up the option of running #1, Antonelli said: "I'll stay with #12 because, obviously, it's a very special number for me, but also it's a way for me to stay grounded, to stay humble.
"I feel like by keeping #12 it allows me to have a new point where to start and build on everything again and try to improve.
"And also, to be honest, I'm very superstitious, and number one has never been a good number for me. Whenever I put it, it went extremely badly. So one more reason to stay with #12."

raw_summary: BYD sold over 300,000 electric vehicles in October, a new record and more than the US managed in the entire third quarter. article_paragraphs: BYD sold over 300,000 electric vehicles in October, a new record and more than the US managed in the entire third quarter.
The world’s leading EV maker is showing no signs of slowing down. BYD sold 490,168 new energy vehicles (NEVs) in October, up 11% from the prior year and the company’s highest monthly total in 2026.
BYD’s battery electric vehicles drove the growth, with a record 305,743 units sold, up 37% year over year and marking the first time its EV sales have crossed the 300,000 mark.
To put that into perspective, just over 262,500 EVs were sold in the US in the entire third quarter combined, according to Kelley Blue Book estimates.

October marked BYD’s sixth straight month of higher sales growth and its third straight month of higher EV sales. Through October, BYD sold 1,953,700 electric vehicles, up 6% from the same period last year.

BYD’s all-electric vehicles (EVs) accounted for about 63% of total sales last month. Plug-in hybrid vehicles, meanwhile, fell 17% in October to 177,382 units. Through October, BYD’s PHEV sales fell 11% to 1,625,969 units.
According to BYD’s filing, the company exported 170,194 vehicles in October as it expands overseas to drive growth in markets like Europe, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America.
Through October, BYD exported over 1.5 million electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles, nearly double compared to last year.

title: Germany's Hydrogen Pipeline Reached Marl. Its Market Still Needs to Add Up

summary: Germany’s hydrogen backbone achieved a genuine milestone on August 4, 2026. RWE and its partners announced that renewable hydrogen produced during commissioning at Lingen had reached Marl Chemical Park , roughly 120 kilometres away. Electrolysers, converted natural gas pipelines and industrial receiving infrastructure were working together.
article_paragraphs: Germany’s hydrogen backbone achieved a genuine milestone on August 4, 2026. RWE and its partners announced that renewable hydrogen produced during commissioning at Lingen had reached Marl Chemical Park , roughly 120 kilometres away. Electrolysers, converted natural gas pipelines and industrial receiving infrastructure were working together.

The GET H2 consortium deserves credit for getting the equipment operating. But completing a hydrogen pipeline and establishing an economically competitive market for the hydrogen moving through it are different achievements.

The announcement did not disclose the quantity received at Marl, the price paid by an industrial customer or which existing hydrogen production was displaced. The English release describes hydrogen being available for industrial use, while the German release says it was used. Neither provides the industrial mass balance needed to determine the actual emissions benefit. The network also contained hydrogen from earlier commissioning activities, which makes tracing individual molecules through the pipeline less useful than measuring what changed at the receiving industrial facilities.

Marl is hardly a new hydrogen customer. The chemical park has used hydrogen for decades in integrated production processes. Providing another source may be useful, especially where renewable hydrogen replaces fossil-derived supply, but existing demand does not automatically become commercially viable demand for a considerably more expensive feedstock.

The larger infrastructure ambition makes that distinction important. Germany’s approved hydrogen core network covers 9,040 kilometres and has expected investment costs of €18.9 billion. Much of the network will use converted natural gas pipelines. These are approved plans and anticipated investments, not evidence that the entire network has been built or that future customers have committed to using it.

There are genuine industrial commitments. RWE has a 15-year agreement with TotalEnergies to supply approximately 30,000 tonnes of renewable hydrogen annually to the Leuna refinery from 2030. That provides a named customer, volume and contract period. The price is undisclosed, and European fuel regulations help create demand for renewable hydrogen in refining.

That is a much stronger commercial signal than commissioning a pipeline. The question is how many comparable customers exist, what they can afford and whether their businesses will continue using hydrogen over the decades required to recover infrastructure investments.

The wider European outlook has become less optimistic. ENTSOG’s October 2026 draft assessment reduced its 2030 hydrogen demand assumption from 620 TWh to 335 TWh, a 46% reduction from its 2024 assessment. Its 2040 assumption fell 33%, from 1,929 TWh to 1,296 TWh. These are changes to European planning scenarios, not measurements of declining actual hydrogen consumption, but they matter when infrastructure economics depend on demand growth.

raw_title: Rivian Is Doing The Damn Thing
title: Rivian Is Doing The Damn Thing
raw_summary: There's never a guarantee a startup car company will actually make it. Automotive history is littered with companies that never made it more than a few years, and after some of Rivian's early financial troubles, it wasn't out of the question that the Irvine, California-based company could join that group. Well, following the introduction of the R2 , those fears seem to be all but squashed. Rivian just posted its third-quarter results for 2026, and the compact-crossover-sized R2 helped raise the automaker's deliveries by 46% year-over-year to 19,248 vehicles, according to Car and Driver . That means Rivian is increasing its yearly sales projection to between 67,000 and 70,000 vehicles — up from 65,000 to 70,000. It also just so happened to outsell the larger and more expensive R1S and R1T flagships combined, as well as the EDV delivery van. I should note that Rivian didn't explicitly say how many R2s it sold, though. This news comes even though the only R2 that Rivian currently sells is the most expensive Performance version of the electric SUV, and the idea that Rivian is still "early in the ramp" of R2 production, according to CEO RJ Scaringe, who spoke with Reuters .

article_paragraphs: There's never a guarantee a startup car company will actually make it. Automotive history is littered with companies that never made it more than a few years, and after some of Rivian's early financial troubles, it wasn't out of the question that the Irvine, California-based company could join that group. Well, following the introduction of the R2 , those fears seem to be all but squashed.

Rivian just posted its third-quarter results for 2026, and the compact-crossover-sized R2 helped raise the automaker's deliveries by 46% year-over-year to 19,248 vehicles, according to Car and Driver . That means Rivian is increasing its yearly sales projection to between 67,000 and 70,000 vehicles — up from 65,000 to 70,000. It also just so happened to outsell the larger and more expensive R1S and R1T flagships combined, as well as the EDV delivery van. I should note that Rivian didn't explicitly say how many R2s it sold, though. This news comes even though the only R2 that Rivian currently sells is the most expensive Performance version of the electric SUV, and the idea that Rivian is still "early in the ramp" of R2 production, according to CEO RJ Scaringe, who spoke with Reuters .

Theoretically, things are only going to get better from here, sales-wise, with the only currently available R2 clocking in at $59,485, including destination. Eventually, a $55,485 Premium trim and $46,485 base model will join its ranks , but the only information we've got is "coming late 2026" and "coming spring 2027," respectively. Of course, even the most expensive R2 is a hell of a lot cheaper than the R1S and R1T, which both start well north of $80,000.

And good news keeps coming, because last week, Scaringe said he was "very confident" Rivian would hit an autonomy milestone this year that would unlock a quarter-billion-dollar tranche of investment money from Uber. That's part of an up-to $1.25 billion investment the rideshare company is making in the automaker through 2031, according to Reuters. It includes an initial $300 million and is contingent on several autonomy milestones. However, Rivian hasn't said exactly what those milestones are. Don't worry, though. Scaringe says Rivian is "right on time."

We do know that the partnership between Uber and Rivian targets the 2028 launch of a driverless R2 robotaxi on Uber's network — starting in a handful of cities and then expanding to about 25 over the next year and a half. Clearly, Rivian is aiming its R2 robotaxi directly at the Tesla Cybercab.

It needs to work, too. As Reuters points out, both the R2's success and the Uber partnership are imperative for making Rivian stick as a company. It's doing pretty well right now, don't get me wrong, but it's still burning through cash like the Bouvier Beale family, and it's looking for any way to narrow those losses.

No matter how you slice it, Rivian is truly showing it's a company that has the ability to stick around and be viable. Once R2 production is fully ramped up and the R3 is introduced, who knows where it could end up? All it needs to do is get that pesky cash burn problem under control.

title: Jackery Launches Explorer 100D Portable Power Station. Maximum Capability For Carryon Compatibility
raw_summary: Jackery just launched the Explorer 100D portable power station. This is Jackery’s smallest battery, giving a new level of versatility to power many of the devices people rely on most. Meanwhile, it integrates the durability and safety people expect from Jackery’s larger models into a compact case.
article_paragraphs: Jackery just launched the Explorer 100D portable power station. This is Jackery’s smallest battery, giving a new level of versatility to power many of the devices people rely on most. Meanwhile, it integrates the durability and safety people expect from Jackery’s larger models into a compact case.

The Explorer 100D has a capacity of 96 Wh (30,000mAh) which puts it just below the carryon limit for domestic and international flights. Meanwhile, up to 158 W of output is more than enough to charge a laptop. The 100D is compatible with advanced protocols including AVS, PD 3.1 and PPS, providing precise charging, particularly for Apple products.

The Explorer 100D measures 4.6” X 3.4” X 3.4”(11.6 X 8.3 cm X 8.5 cm), or about the size of a softball. It weighs 1.87 lbs. (850 g). This is a bit larger than the typical power bank, but much smaller than the typical solar generator. It is also smaller and lighter than the Explorer 100 Plus that it replaces, while also increasing in power output.

On the test sample model, I found the form factor very convenient. It is not small enough to fit in your pants pocket, but the rectangular case with rounded corners was easy to fit in a backpack or carryon bag. A cloth handle makes it easy to hold, and a shoulder strap is available. I had a credentials lanyard from a previous media event on hand, and it worked fine as a strap for the lightweight battery.

On the front of the battery are two 140 W USB-C ports and an 18 W USB-A port. The left USB-C port can both charge the battery and discharge to another device. The battery can also be discharged through the other two ports while it charges. The battery does not come with a charger, although a USB-C cable is provided. I was able to charge the Explorer 100D on a wide range of chargers, although lower powered chargers take a while to charge the large capacity battery.

The front display default shows battery charge percentage as well as input and output power. However, you can switch the display to also show power output to each port or battery health, cycles and temperature.

Unlike some of Jackery’s larger batteries, the 100D does not have cooling fans or vents in the case. The LFP battery is rated for 3000 full charge cycles, good for 8 years of daily use. This is far more durable than many Li-ion power banks, which commonly only offer a few hundred charge cycles. It is also a 50% improvement over the previous Explorer 100 Plus model that it replaces. Of note, while this model does comply with China’s strict CCC (China Compulsory Certification), the logo was not printed on the test model I received, although that may change in the future. Without the logo present, it could be taken away if travelling in China. However, the battery did have FCC and SGS certification printed on it, which are more relevant to most US customers.

The portable battery can function as a solar generator by accepting direct solar input up to 100 W. This makes it a bit different than many power banks. Solar panels connect through the USB-C charge port. which may require the purchase of an adaptor, depending on the panel used. Jackery’s lightweight, folding SolarSaga 100 Air could charge the battery in less than two hours. The battery can also take 12 V or 24V input from a car, boat or RV. Using a traditional USB-C charger, the Explorer 100D can accept up to 140 W of input power.

As a refresher, the new GT 4-Door Coupe is the first model to ride on Mercedes' AMG.EA platform , the second model being the recently revealed GT SUV . In GT55 form its tri-motor powertrain has a peak output of 805 horsepower and 1,372 pound-feet of torque, enough to send it from 0 to 60 mph in 2.4 seconds, while the GT63 ups that to 1,153 hp and 1,475 lb-ft, bringing the 0-60 time down to two seconds flat. Oh yeah, and it'll have an EPA range that gets close to 400 miles, maybe even exceeding that figure.

Ford wants its sales back to pre-pandemic levels, and it has a new approach that CEO Jim Farley hopes will get the company there: Make cars that are actually interesting. Wild concept, I know, but perhaps it is just crazy enough to work. From the Wall Street Journal :
Ford Motor expects to sell 5 million cars a year by early next decade, Chief Executive Jim Farley told workers this week, a sales volume the company hasn't reached since before the pandemic.

The company's global strategy turns on Farley's emphasis to no longer make "boring" vehicles, which for now has left it without the budget-friendly small sedans and SUVs it used to give priority to. Farley has said that making affordable vehicles remains a priority, however, and Ford is planning to launch five new models priced below $40,000 by the end of the decade, including an all-electric pickup truck.

Ford once decided to kill off nearly all its interesting cars in favor of making crossover slop, so this will be a reversal of that. Of course, the crossover slop got Ford to the sales numbers it's now trying to return to, so who knows what's best.

Michigan's race for Senate is a closely-watched one, and it's made headlines recently as (former?) Democrat Haley Stevens turned away from supporting her (former?) party-mate Abdul El-Sayed to go back Republican Mike Rogers. But within Michigan, there's another factor playing in voters' minds: The trade war with Canada. From Automotive News :
The Michigan seat is crucial for Democrats to get a Senate majority. It's also a race where Trump's trade war with Canada has become a ballot box issue.

article_paragraphs: US voters rarely, if ever, get a chance to vote on someone whose name is not on the ballot, but this year is an exceptional one with Tesla CEO Elon Musk throwing millions at key races. In years past, Musk’s seal of approval would be a planet-saving badge of climate action honor for candidates seeking office. Now he’s just another highly privileged crank exercising his outsized financial power against transgender rights. Who’d a thunk it?

Coincidentally or not, Elon Musk’s highly personal vendetta against transgender rights has materialized against the backdrop of a corresponding focus in Republican Party campaign strategy, with one early hint being his “pronouns suck” message on Twitter in July of 2020.
Musk went on to buy Twitter and rename it “X” in 2022, and the rest is transphobic history .

Also coincidentally or not, the Republican Party has been hammering against human and civil rights for generations, but the razor-sharp focus on transgender persons did not bloom into full flower until 2021, after US President Donald Trump lost his first bid for re-election.

In the aftermath of Trump’s failed insurrection of January 6, the Party alighted upon transgender rights as a powerful tool in a coordinated campaign strategy aimed at ginning up the fevered emotions of voters already besotted with US President Trump’s “MAGA” propaganda during his first term in office.

In addition to working the conservative aisle of the US Supreme Court, the anti-transgender movement has focused on legislation introduced by state lawmakers (looking at you, Florida ). Among the LGBTQ+ organizations tracking the bills is the organization is the Human Rights Campaign, which has identified a distinct shift in anti-transgender strategy during the 2020 campaign cycle.

All else being equal, transgender persons are an unlikely target for a national political campaign. According to one study, self-identified transgender persons over the age of 13 make up just 1% of the US population , with much of the self-reporting cohort under age 35. As for the much-ballyhooed danger of transgender-related surgery on minors, that is vanishingly rare to the point of not occurring at all according to a 2024 Harvard study. Somewhat ironically, the same study found a “substantially higher” rate of sex-affirming surgery among non-transgender minors and adults .
For that matter, Elon Musk is known to have availed himself of body-affirming treatments as an adult, but that’s a whole ‘nother can of worms.

title: Lexus is taking a page from China for its next electric SUV launching in 2027
raw_summary: Toyota’s luxury brand Lexus is launching a new electric SUV in 2027, its first vehicle built in China in over two decades. It’s official. Toyota is breaking from tradition, planning to develop and produce the new vehicle in China rather than its home market of Japan.
summary: Toyota’s luxury brand Lexus is launching a new electric SUV in 2027, its first vehicle built in China in over two decades. Toyota is breaking from tradition, planning to develop and produce the new vehicle in China rather than its home market of Japan.
article_paragraphs: Toyota’s luxury brand Lexus is launching a new electric SUV in 2027, its first vehicle built in China in over two decades.
It’s official. Toyota is breaking from tradition, planning to develop and produce the new vehicle in China rather than its home market of Japan.
Lexus confirmed the new vehicle will be made at its new manufacturing plant in Jinshan, Shanghai, and will go on sale in 2027.
As the first Lexus factory built from scratch overseas, the company said the new plant will bring together its global manufacturing capabilities.

Toyota broke ground on the facility in June 2025, saying the new facility will unlock “Lexus speed” as it aims to keep pace with domestic brands like BYD. Construction was expected to be completed this past August, with the first vehicle scheduled to roll off the assembly line in the fall of 2027.
The first Lexus model will be an electric SUV, produced using advanced manufacturing methods such as gigacasting to reduce costs and speed up output.
The facility will be a cornerstone of Toyota’s comeback plans in China, where it’s struggled to compete with local brands.
Production capacity will be around 1,000 units per month in 2027 as Toyota ramps up to “tens of thousands” in 2028.

article_paragraphs: Formula 1’s new world champion Kimi Antonelli has “made everyone look silly” in 2026, according to outgoing champion Lando Norris.

Antonelli became the 2026 champion by finishing third in the Mexican Grand Prix and his title celebrations were playing out on screens next to where drivers were conducting their post-race media debriefs.
There was plenty of praise from his F1 rivals and genuine appreciation for what he’s been able to achieve this year.
“Unbelievable, what he’s done; he’s blown everyone away. I hope everyone gives him enough credit for what he’s achieved this year,” Norris said.

“He’s made everyone else look silly. He’s driven that well, and he’s been able to click with his car. He’s worked hard to understand how to drive this car, and he’s exploited it better than anyone else. He deserves every single bit of success. He deserves these moments he’s doing now and celebrating.

“It’s even more impressive that it’s only his second season in Formula 1. He’s 20 years old. It’s incredible. I’m very happy for him. I’m very happy to see my number one go over to him, because he deserves it. I’m, in a way, happy to see it go.”
Norris added: “He has a very strong team-mate [George Russell], but he’s beaten him the whole time, the whole season.

“[You can] count how many mistakes he’s made this season - I don’t even think you could put it on [all five fingers of] one hand, honestly. He’s come from the back of the grid. He’s won from the front. He’s done everything he needs to do. He’s been there every single race. That’s something that no other driver can say they’ve done this season.

article_paragraphs: Electric trucks made up 50.3% of all heavy trucks sold in China in September. That’s 33,100 electric big rigs in a single month, up 37% from a year ago, while the overall heavy-truck market shrank by 21%.
And it’s showing up in the oil data. China’s diesel demand is on track to fall by about 230,000 barrels per day this year, and trucks running on batteries and natural gas are doing most of the work.
In 2024, new-energy vehicles accounted for 13.6% of heavy trucks (12 tonnes and up) sold in China. In 2025, sales nearly tripled to 231,100 units, up 182%, for a 28.9% share.
December 2025 hit 53.9%, but that was a rush. Buyers piled in before trade-in subsidies expired and new purchase tax costs kicked in, and the share dropped back to about 23% by March.

Then it came right back. Through the first nine months of 2026, China sold 226,400 electric heavy trucks, up 64%, for a 38.1% share. That’s already almost as many as in all of 2025, with a quarter still to go. In tractors, the big rigs that pull long-haul trailers, the September share hit 64.5%.

That’s well ahead of Beijing’s own plan. This year, 11 government bodies set a target of 40% new-energy heavy-truck sales by 2030, along with 1.6 million of them on the road, 30,000 km of zero-carbon freight corridors and about 3,000 charging and swap stations. The market blew past that sales target four years early on a monthly basis, and CATL now says new-energy trucks will be half of China’s annual truck sales by 2028.
It comes down to cost. In most uses, an electric heavy truck in China is now cheaper to own and run than a diesel one, and fleets run that math every day.

CATL claims savings of about 0.6 yuan per km. Independent numbers are more measured, but still favorable: a study by the ICCT and China’s CATARC found battery-electric trucks about 19% cheaper per tonne-km than diesel in good conditions, though they lose that edge at low annual mileage or when battery weight eats into payload.

raw_title: Cybertruck Could Get Trick Suspension-Based Loading Ramp
title: Cybertruck Could Get Trick Suspension-Based Loading Ramp
raw_summary: Loading a truck can be tricky if the cargo is heavy or awkward, like with a motorcycle. Tesla might have a novel solution, based on a patent application published a week ago that puts the trick suspension system in the Cybertruck — including the new low-cost model — to work. At the owner's command, it would raise the front of the truck, lower the rear, and make access to the bed that much easier. Patent application number US 2026/0326744 A1, titled 'Adjustable Suspension For A Vehicle', details a 'ramp mode' that independently adjusts the suspension at each wheel. The drawings use the familiar wedge-shaped pickup, but it's worth noting that Tesla describes the technology broadly rather than exclusively for the Cybertruck. Tilting the truck changes the angle where a ramp would meet the bed, which could make loading an ATV or motorcycle easier. Tesla also says lowering the rear would allow owners to use a shorter ramp. In one example, the automaker proposes raising the front of the truck by 80 mm (3.1 inches) while lowering the rear by 70 mm (2.8 inches) to reduce the ramp-to-bed breakover angle.

Tilting the truck changes the angle where a ramp would meet the bed, which could make loading an ATV or motorcycle easier. Tesla also says lowering the rear would allow owners to use a shorter ramp. In one example, the automaker proposes raising the front of the truck by 80 mm (3.1 inches) while lowering the rear by 70 mm (2.8 inches) to reduce the ramp-to-bed breakover angle.

Tilting the bed sounds reasonable, but the payoff is in how much it changes the loading equation. According to Tesla, the angle where the ramp meets the bed could drop from 45–55 degrees to 20–30 degrees. Tesla says owners would be able to adjust individual corners of the suspension on uneven ground and control everything from an onboard interface or smartphone. Included safeguards would keep the vehicle in Park, automatically apply the parking brake, and prevent shifts into Drive, Reverse, or Neutral while 'ramp mode' is active.

Sensor inputs could block or delay a suspension adjustment if conditions make it unsuitable. Other proposed settings include a 'dump mode', which lowers all four corners to bring the truck bed within easier reach, and a leveling mode intended for activities such as camping or tailgating on uneven ground. Interestingly, in November 2019, Tesla filed a patent application for an adjustable vehicle suspension. It featured similar ideas, so in a way, this is the company simply continuing the slow march toward patent acquisition and potentially production.

Of course, a key point here is that this is just a patent application. Like plenty of other patent applications, there's no telling if this ever makes it into production. That said, when we uncovered patents for Tesla's fan-assisted suction system and adjustable rear spoiler for the Roadster around a month ago, the company confirmed both were slated for production during the wild Roadster demo in mid-October. Those were practical engineering exercises and this new way of loading a bed seems to follow in line.

title: Which Automaker Has The Coolest Model Names?
raw_summary: Many car enthusiasts tend to view their car more as a family member than an appliance . Cars take us to some of the most important events in our lives, to some of the most memorable places in our lives, and hell, for a lot of us, they're the second place we ever see right after we're thrust into human existence and we leave the hospitals where we were born. To me, family members have names , not alphanumeric codes , so I've always preferred when automakers give their cars proper names. There's no cutoff date for this one, mostly because I think a lot of the coolest model names have been discontinued or replaced with alphanumeric nonsense, so feel free to unearth some obscure carmaker that hasn't made a car in a century or something, as long as they had cool model names. Sound off in the comments section below!

In a rare change of pace, Lincoln went from using lame alphanumeric model names like MKZ and MKX to what I believe are the coolest model names in the industry. To clarify, the company started off with proper names for most of its models throughout the 20th century, but for some reason Lincoln decided to ditch those in the 2000s, which I lamented, even then as a child.

With current names like Corsair, Nautilus, Aviator, and Navigator, the modern lineup is stacked with heavy hitters, but Lincoln's classic names are really good, too. Of course there's also the classic Continental, and my beloved Zephyr. Corsair makes me think of the Vought F4U Corsair warbird. Nautilus makes me think of the prehistoric undersea chambered mollusk that has barely evolved over the past couple million years, and Zephyr evokes images of Art Deco-era pie-in-the-sky inventions like early flying machines and trains. All of this imagery comes from the exciting and fascinating names given to Lincoln's cars, which is something that alphanumeric names just don't quite achieve in my brain. The new Lectric XP4 Limited Editions come in three flavors: District, (black) Jubilee (pink), and Ridge (green). Each is priced at $1,399 and includes a 750W motor, upgraded accessories, and a distinctive matte paint job. That’s just a $100 premium over the existing XP 750, yet comes with a whole new host of accessories designed specifically for each special edition model.
So while the underlying bike remains largely unchanged from the bones of the XP 750, the new packages are designed to make the XP4 even more useful straight out of the box.
The District edition is aimed squarely at urban commuters, sporting a stealthy Matte Black finish and an accessory package designed for daily transportation.

That includes two waterproof pannier bags, a redesigned LevelUp rear cargo rack, a heavy-duty bike lock, and an upgraded high-output headlight. There’s also a fast charger, suspension seat post with comfort saddle, and handlebar phone mount.
It’s essentially a ready-made commuter setup, particularly for riders looking to replace some of their car trips with an e-bike.

The Jubilee edition takes a more casual approach, arriving in a distinctive Matte Thistle colorway. Designed for neighborhood cruising, weekend errands, and trips to the local farmers market, it swaps the commuter-focused panniers for a front and rear cargo package and a small roll-top bag.

title: Kimi Antonelli Becomes Youngest-Ever F1 World Champion
raw_summary: For the first time since 1953, an Italian is the F1 World Drivers' Champion. Kimi Antonelli finished third at the Mexico City Grand Prix on Sunday, clinching the championship. The 20-year-old Mercedes driver also became F1's youngest-ever champion, surpassing the mark set by a 23-year-old Sebastian Vettel in 2010. With Antonelli never crossing the finish line lower than fifth so far this season, the ninth-place finish he needed to secure his maiden title seemed like a cakewalk. However, nothing is ever guaranteed in Formula 1. Antonelli was never in contention for the win at Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez , but that didn't matter. His main goal was getting home in one piece. The young Italian qualified fourth and stayed there before cycling to the lead during the pit stop. He would eventually have to yield the position to make his own stop on Lap 43. He could've held the lead if he stayed out on lap longer. Valtteri Bottas' Cadillac suffered a catastrophic left-front suspension failure while heading into Turn 1. The machine became a sled, slid through the run-off area and slammed into the barrier. It took a while for Bottas to get out of the cockpit, but he walked away. Race control was forced to throw a red flag to recover his car.

The 20-year-old Mercedes driver also became F1's youngest-ever champion, surpassing the mark set by a 23-year-old Sebastian Vettel in 2010.
article_paragraphs: For the first time since 1953, an Italian is the F1 World Drivers' Champion. Kimi Antonelli finished third at the Mexico City Grand Prix on Sunday, clinching the championship. The 20-year-old Mercedes driver also became F1's youngest-ever champion, surpassing the mark set by a 23-year-old Sebastian Vettel in 2010. With Antonelli never crossing the finish line lower than fifth so far this season, the ninth-place finish he needed to secure his maiden title seemed like a cakewalk. However, nothing is ever guaranteed in Formula 1.

Antonelli was never in contention for the win at Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez , but that didn't matter. His main goal was getting home in one piece. The young Italian qualified fourth and stayed there before cycling to the lead during the pit stop. He would eventually have to yield the position to make his own stop on Lap 43. He could've held the lead if he stayed out on lap longer. Valtteri Bottas' Cadillac suffered a catastrophic left-front suspension failure while heading into Turn 1. The machine became a sled, slid through the run-off area and slammed into the barrier. It took a while for Bottas to get out of the cockpit, but he walked away. Race control was forced to throw a red flag to recover his car.

Back in fourth for the standing restart, Antonelli took advantage of Charles Leclerc locking up into Turn 1 to snag the final podium spot. He may have finished third behind Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton , but the celebration under a blizzard of confetti might be the most memorable of the Italian's entire career. After the trophies were handed out and the champagne sprayed, Hamilton and Verstappen hoisted the new champion up onto their shoulders in front of the roaring crowd. It was the Hollywood freeze-frame ending to Antonelli's meteoric ascent to racing's highest summit.

It was a disastrous day on the other side of the garage. George Russell started 2nd, but had a power unit deployment issue on the opening run to Turn 1 and sank down the order. He then made contact with Isack Hadjar in Turn 6 and received a ten-second penalty for his trouble. Russell salvaged a sixth-place finish. While the British driver didn't hesitate to congratulate Antonelli after they climbed out of their cars, it was clear he was devastated to lose the championship to his teammate. Russell skipped the mandatory post-race media interviews. In Russell's absence, Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff heaped praise on Antonelli and the team's patience with the sophomore champion, saying:

"People said he shouldn't even be in F1, he should be at a smaller team, 10 races and no points, the tears in Spa, and then this. I'm just so proud for the team, all of them continued to trust him and he delivered."

The tumult at Scuderia Ferrari reached a new low. Ferrari seemed poised to take the victory with Lewis Hamilton taking his first pole since 2023. With how difficult it is to pass in Mexico City, the seven-time champion just needed to survive the start's lengthy run to Turn 1. His biggest threat turned out to be his own teammate. Leclerc slipstreamed from third to Hamilton, then tried to pass on the outside. The Monégasque driver took another shot at the lead heading into Turn 4.

Neither Ferrari driver kept their car on the track through Turn 4. While Hamilton re-entered the racing surface to make Turn 5, Leclerc cut the course across the grass to take the lead. Ferrari would ask the pair to swap positions to avoid a penalty, but this time was different. Max Verstappen had gotten past Hamilton. Ferrari and Leclerc opted to put their fates in the stewards' hands rather than yield the lead by choice. The decision: a five-second time penalty.

The penalty was enough for Verstappen to inherit the lead after pit stops, but not enough for Hamilton to take second. The decision's light-handedness was something Hamilton noted after the race, adding that he received a ten-second penalty for a similar infraction last year. He was far less calm during the red flag, telling his team over the radio, "We've got big problems. Big, big problems." After Hamilton returned to pit lane, he stormed off the back of the garage

raw_title: Giugiaro Revisits The Baby Lambo He Invented
title: Giugiaro Revisits The Baby Lambo He Invented
raw_summary: The Lamborghini Gallardo might have given way to the Huracan and the Temerario with its many variants , but it is remembered as one of Sant'Agata's most popular models that helped the company break through. The production supercar was introduced in 2003, but its development actually started in the '90s. Now, the designer of the concept — Fabrizio Giugiaro — has teamed up CAVËN Atelier to create a limited-production restomod. You might remember that the Gallardo was signed off by Luc Donckerwolke. However, its design was an evolution of the Calà concept from 1995, which was penned by Italdesign. Giugiaro had also created an early version of the Gallardo in 1998, which reportedly didn't change much as it transitioned to production. Fast forward to 2026 and CAVËN Atelier has unveiled a reworked version of the Italian supercar, giving its designer access to modern engineering, materials, and technology. The Hommage 26 is based on a Gallardo donor vehicle, adding a redesigned exterior, small interior tweaks, a revised suspension setup, and an upgraded V10 powertrain which is mated to a manual gearbox.

Now, the designer of the concept — Fabrizio Giugiaro — has teamed up CAVËN Atelier to create a limited-production restomod. You might remember that the Gallardo was signed off by Luc Donckerwolke.

However, its design was an evolution of the Calà concept from 1995, which was penned by Italdesign. Giugiaro had also created an early version of the Gallardo in 1998, which reportedly didn't change much as it transitioned to production. Fast forward to 2026 and CAVËN Atelier has unveiled a reworked version of the Italian supercar, giving its designer access to modern engineering, materials, and technology. The Hommage 26 is based on a Gallardo donor vehicle, adding a redesigned exterior, small interior tweaks, a revised suspension setup, and an upgraded V10 powertrain which is mated to a manual gearbox.

Visually, the supercar is instantly recognizable as a Gallardo, although most body panels are new and made of carbon fiber. The highlight is the connection between the headlights and the front bumper intakes, something that was not technically feasible at the time. Other notable changes include the pop-down headlight units, 20-inch alloy wheels, redesigned taillights with modern LED graphics, dual active rear spoilers, and dual exhaust pipes above a body-colored diffuser.

The interior looks similar to the donor vehicle, but gains small touches like Alcantara upholstery on the dashboard, a rear window that opens to enhance the audio experience, and a hexagon motif on the door cards with red stitching. Predictably, upgrades go deeper than skin. As reported by Classic Driver , CAVËN Atelier will offer the naturally-aspirated V10 engine with two different outputs, producing 540 and 560 horsepower, respectively. This is more than the 493 hp of the standard Gallardo but significantly less than the 907 hp of the electrified Temerario. More importantly, the engine is mated to a six-speed manual gearbox, which is not available in the Gallardo's successors.

The Hommage 26 was unveiled at the Concours at Wynn Las Vegas, as the first chapter of the brand's Designer Series. CAVËN Atelier will build 25 examples, with a starting price of €900,000 ($1,008,800) excluding the donor vehicle. The latter currently ranges from around $75,000 to more than $500,000 depending on condition, meaning that the total price of the restomod could reach $1.5 million. The company has confirmed that similar projects are already in the works, with original designers revisiting models from the late '90s and early '00s.

The conversions will target collectors, given the steep pricing and limited production, but CAVËN Atelier insists they are intended to be driven rather than preserved in climate-controlled garages. What's interesting is that the Hommage 26 is not the first Gallardo restomod out there. The Etna supercar, from Tedson Motors, arrived in 2025 with modern design features and suspension components from the Super Trofeo racecar.

title: At $7,500, Will This 2003 Jeep Wrangler Sahara Get Its Just Dessert?
raw_summary: Introduced in the 1940s, the Willys Jeep has long been hailed as the "truck that won the war." Let's see whether any of that DNA remains in today's Nice Price or No Dice Wrangler and, if so, whether its price wins our admiration. It's almost unheard of for an automobile model to switch from one end driving to the other, but that has happened on at least two occasions. It's almost unheard of for an automobile model to switch from one end driving to the other, but that has happened on at least two occasions. Another notable example of an existing model switching driving ends is the Polestar 2, which, with its 2024 refresh, changed its base single-motor layout from front- to rear-wheel-drive.

The 2024 Polestar 2 Long Range we looked at last Friday proved that point moot as the model offers dual motors driving both ends. It also had the model's biggest battery, a desirable driving assistance package, and, at $22,995, seemingly unfathomable depreciation. That latter affliction might be because Polestar sales are currently being banned in the U.S. due to the model's China origins, with owners possibly wanting out before the parts situation becomes dire. Regardless of threats of impending doom, our Polestar's condition and price had a number of you willing to take the chance—hypothetically, of course—earning the EV a respectable 66% 'Nice Price' win.

The name Sahara comes from Arabic, where it means "desert." Of course, that means we shouldn't call the world's largest non-polar desert the "Sahara Desert," since that is redundant. It's the same thing as calling Los Angeles' ancient fossil graveyard the "La Brea Tar Pits," since that is literally "The Tar Tar Pits."

Jeep chose the Sahara name for one of the myriad trim levels and special editions applied to the TJ Wrangler over its 10-year model run. The Sahara package included body-color fender extenders, full doors, cloth upholstery, and five-spoke alloy wheels.

This 2003 Jeep Wrangler Sahara is painted in Sienna Pearl matched to a gray hardtop and interior trim. Its running boards and outer bumper caps were likely once black but, due to the sun's daily attacks, have also faded to a similar gray hue. Other indicators of this Jeep's age include a cracked and dented right-front fender and rust bubbling through on both front wings. Fortunately, those are bolt-ons, and replacements are readily available from places like Amazon and eBay, making these aesthetic imperfections easy to address.

The rest of the Jeep appears to be in good condition, with the seller noting the frame and the rest of the bodywork are free of rust. That's a big deal, considering this TJ is offered in Pennsylvania, arguably the crusty buckle on the Rust Belt.

Another attractive aspect of this TJ is its removable hard top. Yes, removing or replacing the top is a job that'll take two (or three) people to complete, but it really makes this a four-season ride. The seller does warn, however, that while the A/C works fine, the heater is non-functional, so all passengers should be forewarned to bundle up in inclement weather.

article_paragraphs: The Trailfinder and the Trackfinder by Nismo Nick are two wildly different takes on the ladder-frame SUV for SEMA

Following up on last year's V8-powered Xterra restomod , automotive enthusiast and builder Nicholas Scherr – also known as "Nismo Nick" – is returning to SEMA with a pair of custom Nissan SUVs. The Trailfinder and Trackfinder celebrate the 40th anniversary of the Pathfinder, pushing the platform in two wildly opposing directions.

Instead of modifying the current iteration of the model, Nismo Nick chose the older R51 Pathfinder as the starting point for his unique creations. This makes sense at it was the last generation of the Pathfinder to ride on a rugged ladder frame chassis, before the nameplate switched to car-like unibody underpinnings.

As with the Projext X from last year, the new builds wear components from the current D41-generation Nissan Frontier, in a quest to modernize their appearance inside-out. Frontier-sourced parts include the grille, LED headlights, front fenders, front doors, LED taillights, dashboard, center console, and door panels.
Another common feature between the two is the Ruby Slate Pearl paint which is borrowed from the 2021 Nissan Maxima 40th Anniversary sedan.

Starting with the Trackfinder, it adds Nismo flavor to the Pathfinder, taking inspiration from the GMC Typhoon. The model sits closer to the ground, and rides on a new set of forged 20-inch wheels finished in black. Behind the then-spoke design we can see the cross-drilled and slotted brake discs clamped by red calipers.

Besides the Frontier face swap with glossy black trim and red accents, the Trackfinder gets special logos on the front doors, red and white stripes on the profile, a Seibon carbon fiber hood with a prominent scoop, a rear spoiler, and quadruple tailpipes sticking out of the rear bumper.

Power comes from a 4.0-liter V6 engine upgraded with a Z1 Off-Road supercharger, custom carbon fiber intake piping, a heat-shielded airbox, and an UpRev tune. As a result, the output has nearly double to a respectable 501 hp (374 kW / 508 PS). Another cool touch is the Xterra-sourced six-speed manual gearbox featuring a Centerforce clutch and flywheel.

As usual, you can ask your questions about Edd's rankings by commenting on this post in The Race Members' Club - and have a crack at compiling your own Mexican GP tier list with our handy visual tool !

Max Verstappen raced with his usual incisive brilliance, showing strong pace and outstanding decision-making at the starts and in keeping Hamilton behind. On top of that, he was also central to Red Bull's recovery after a difficult Friday.

In many circumstances, the lock-up that ruined his last qualifying lap would have denied him a place in this tier, but the mitigating circumstances of traffic's contribution to that save him - even though the one-place grid penalty for Friday nonsense with Liam Lawson is also a small negative that in other circumstances might have bumped him to a lower tier.

Ryo Hirakawa 's unique circumstances mean he has to be judged by what would normally be generous standards for the job he did after taking over Esteban Ocon's seat. He was flirting with reaching Q2 before hitting Alex Albon's turbulent air in the middle sector of his final Q1 run, meaning the gap to Bearman was exaggerated. He then drove a combative race, passing both the Williams drivers late on, for a well-deserved point once penalties were applied.

Liam Lawson recovered from setbacks to score points. He started from the pits but despite the red flag timing not helping him, he made steady progress then surged from 15th at the standing restart to take what was ultimately the midfield win after penalties were applied.

For Lewis Hamilton , this was a strong weekend save for his part in the Turn 4 moment where both drivers braked too late to make the corner. Had he avoided that, he would likely swap places with Verstappen. His first pole position since 2023 was also brilliantly-taken.

title: Ford launches a 'privacy promise' and explains how and why it uses customer data
raw_summary: As Ford prepares to launch a new generation of connected cars, the automaker is making a public promise about how it will handle that information. The company unveiled on Monday what it calls a “privacy promise” — an “explicit commitment” to keep customers’ vehicle data safe and give them control over what they share. Ford also launched a website designed to educate customers about how, where, and why the automakers uses their data, and to show them how to change those settings.

The company unveiled on Monday what it calls a “privacy promise” — an “explicit commitment” to keep customers’ vehicle data safe and give them control over what they share.
article_paragraphs: As Ford prepares to launch a new generation of connected cars, the automaker is making a public promise about how it will handle that information.

The company unveiled on Monday what it calls a “privacy promise” — an “explicit commitment” to keep customers’ vehicle data safe and give them control over what they share. Ford also launched a website designed to educate customers about how, where, and why the automakers uses their data, and to show them how to change those settings.

While those controls have existed for years now, Ford wants to communicate more clearly with its customers about them, especially ahead of the launch of new, more connected vehicles like the ones being built on its upcoming “universal electric vehicle” platform.

“I personally think that it’s super important for us to be making it very clear to our customers what our data practices are, and not only that, but making a commitment to them about it,” Ford’s chief privacy officer Kristin Jones said in an interview with TechCrunch. “I also see this as a great opportunity to educate our customers about how they share data.”

This new privacy push comes as automakers are making their cars increasingly connected. While some polling shows U.S. customers want the kinds of features enabled by this connectivity , such as remote start, navigation, and driver-assistance software, only 14% said they fully understand what data their vehicle collects.

That has left room for some companies to quietly sell that data to third parties — a practice that got General Motors in trouble with the Federal Trade Commission, and also resulted in a $220 million settlement with 36 states last week .

This lack of consumer awareness around data collection and sharing has also opened the door for other companies to market themselves as better stewards of customer data. Slate Auto, the EV startup backed by Jeff Bezos, has made that pitch ahead of the expected launch of its minimalist pickup truck later this year.

“We did a survey of 1,000 consumers, and 91% of them said that data privacy was a key consideration for them. Realistically, it’s not something they engage with every day, but they want to know that they’re, again, in control, and that they have access to the information they need there,” Jones said. “I wouldn’t comment on what our competitors are doing, or anything that’s sort of been in the news there, but certainly it’s something that people don’t trust companies to take care with their data, and we really want to make sure we’re building that trust relationship with them.”

raw_summary: You don't need me to tell you this, but I'm still going to say it: Cars are more expensive now than ever before . If you're a member of the 1%, then you probably couldn't care less about this, but for the remaining 99% of the people living in the United States, it makes the already costly prospect of car buying an even spendier endeavor. Unfortunately, even the old trick of buying used cars to save money is less effective than it once was, since used car prices are higher than ever, too , and used cars don't always come with the peace of mind that a new, warrantied car does. That's where CarMax comes in, as its business model relies on selling used cars that SAE-certified technicians have inspected over 125 components on, and if that's not enough, you can pay for an extended warranty. The downside of CarMax is that its used cars tend to be more expensive than used cars from other dealerships or private sellers, and there's no haggling room in its prices (which is either a pro or a con, depending on your persuasion). Even if you're not ready to pay CarMax prices for a used car, though, it still pays to check the retailer's inventory, since not only don't you have to negotiate, they're picky about what they sell.

If finding the cheapest car around is your top priority, then CarMax isn't going to be the best place to start your search. If, however, you're sick of getting the runaround from other dealerships or you're burnt out from the dreaded act of haggling with private sellers, then the benefits of buying from CarMax may outweigh the drawbacks.

Every last vehicle in CarMax's national inventory has never experienced flood or frame damage, never has a salvage history, and never has odometer discrepancies. Every CarMax purchase includes a 10-day money-back guarantee, as well as at least a 30-day limited warranty, which may be longer depending on where you live. And they're all offered with CarMax's MaxCare warranty, which, for an extra cost, can extend up to five years after the purchase date on most cars.

I bought my 2017 Mini Cooper S four-door from CarMax in 2020, and I ended up buying the five-year extended warranty because I did not want to be on the hook for European car repair prices. Yes, the initial purchase price was higher than I would've paid at a normal dealership, or from a private party, but I really wanted the peace of mind provided by a warranty, and I have no regrets.

I ended up using the warranty several times over the course of my five-year contract, and I never had any trouble getting repairs covered, from replacing an engine mount to replacing a water pump to replacing a wobbly sunroof switch and a few other, smaller issues. It all depends on your priorities, but it never hurts to look at all options in front of you.

raw_title: How Europe’s battery passport could have a big impact on US e-bikes
title: How Europe's battery passport could have a big impact on US e-bikes
raw_summary: Europe is preparing to introduce a new requirement that could change how electric bicycle batteries are tracked, repaired, recycled, and potentially even resold. Starting in February 2027, new e-bike batteries sold in the European Union will be required to carry a digital battery passport, giving each battery its own digital identity and making important information about its origins and characteristics accessible throughout its lifetime. And while the rules are European, their impact could eventually reach American e-bike riders, too.
summary: Europe is preparing to introduce a new requirement that could change how electric bicycle batteries are tracked, repaired, recycled, and potentially even resold. Starting in February 2027, new e-bike batteries sold in the European Union will be required to carry a digital battery passport, giving each battery its own digital identity and making important information about its origins and characteristics accessible throughout its lifetime.
article_paragraphs: Europe is preparing to introduce a new requirement that could change how electric bicycle batteries are tracked, repaired, recycled, and potentially even resold. Starting in February 2027, new e-bike batteries sold in the European Union will be required to carry a digital battery passport, giving each battery its own digital identity and making important information about its origins and characteristics accessible throughout its lifetime.
And while the rules are European, their impact could eventually reach American e-bike riders, too.

The battery passport requirement comes from the EU’s 2023 Batteries Regulation , which established new standards for battery sustainability, traceability, and transparency. The rules cover several categories of batteries, including those used in electric cars, electric bicycles, electric scooters, and other light electric vehicles.

Beginning February 18, 2027, newly placed batteries in these categories will need digital passports accessible through QR codes. Scanning the code will provide access to information about the battery, though exactly what users can see will depend on their authorization level.

The information can include details such as the battery’s manufacturer, chemistry, capacity, cycle count, carbon footprint, and materials used in its construction. The system also provides for information about battery performance and durability, including data related to battery health and degradation.

Anyone who has purchased a used electric bicycle knows that the battery is often one of the biggest unknowns. A bike might look nearly new, but its battery could have hundreds of charge cycles under its belt and significantly reduced capacity.
Even a quick test ride before a secondhand e-bike purchase may fail to demonstrate just how little capacity remains in a heavily used battery.
With replacement e-bike batteries costing hundreds of dollars, that’s a pretty important detail.

The KTM was a decent bike to have at Sepang, with the low grip and the hard braking and the manufacturer's successful work on tyre longevity.

It still wasn't quite enough for Acosta to forgo a strategy of brazenly shadowing Marquez in Q2 - but this felt like an x-factor that brought Acosta's weekend together, yielding a front-row spot that looked implausible otherwise.
He parlayed that into a race biding his time behind Ai Ogura in the sprint and then striking for the win, then shrugged off going down to sixth in the main race to recover to an eventual second.

He had the pace for second anyway, but that first lap was very pleasing - around the outside of Marco Bezzecchi into Turn 4, an opportunistic mugging of Enea Bastianini into Turn 7, and a tidy lunge on Ogura into the final corner.

Marquez now has one hand and several fingers on a record-equalling eighth MotoGP championship trophy. It was the Phillip Island sprint win (and Jorge Martin injury) that had swung it clearly in his favour - but acknowledging that, this was a stylish coup de grâce that suggested he might have been unbeatable anyway.

A suboptimal condition of the asphalt that was supposed to be resurfaced but wasn't probably helped Marquez, who found a great groove in the opening session (lead Ducati by nine tenths) and was never far from the top spot over the rest of the weekend.

article_paragraphs: Kimi Antonelli is Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion, aged just 20 and in only his second season on the grid.
Here's what we make of his achievement and his 2026 performance, our ripostes to some of his critics, and what we're hoping to see from Antonelli next.
There was never any doubt about Antonelli's pace potential, but for him to win the championship with few major errors is remarkable.
Aside from crashing in FP3 in Australia and clipping the inside wall at Turn 1 in Baku qualifying, he's been remarkably clean for a young driver in only his second season.

Yes, there are still rough edges to smooth out, as exhibited by his tendency to flirt dangerously with track limits. But that's something he's working on, and Austin showed he's making progress. And as he tidies up these aspects of his game and bolts it on to his underlying pace and the almost Fernando Alonso-esque relentlessness he can show in races he will become increasingly formidable.
That's what is remarkable about Antonelli's achievement. He's nowhere near the finished article he will become with more experience, but even in this unrefined form he's performed outstandingly.
Don't be fooled by the narrative some will spin about the crushing dominance of the Mercedes.

Yes, it's been the strongest all-round package, but team-mate George Russell's struggles prove that getting the best out of it and adapting to the new regulations is not easy. And Antonelli put an enormous amount of work into doing so on top of any advantage he may have had in default driving style over Russell.

raw_title: 7 Luxury Vehicles From Throughout History That Used 4-Cylinder Engines
title: 7 Luxury Vehicles From Throughout History That Used 4-Cylinder Engines
raw_summary: Luxury cars can differ massively from one another, but most of us make similar assumptions when describing the term "luxury car." We picture leather seats, 20-plus-inch chrome wheels, full-size silhouettes, and big displacement engines with a lot of cylinders . However, every once in a while, automakers mix things up a little and throw in an ingredient you might not expect. Four-cylinder engines are one such ingredient, and they found themselves in luxury cars from an assortment of automakers, spanning across what is almost the entire history of the automobile so far. We're talking Fiats from the turn of the 20th century, British executive sedans produced by Rover in the late '60s and early '70s, hybridized BMW 5 Series sedans, Range Rover SUVs, and more. What's interesting here is that, for the most part, all of these cars were and are considered successes, with rare exceptions (Facel Vega Facellia, we're looking at you), which suggests luxury car buyers aren't actually all that hung up on the engine under the hood. Without further ado, here are our seven four-cylinder luxury cars, in chronological order.

We're talking Fiats from the turn of the 20th century, British executive sedans produced by Rover in the late '60s and early '70s, hybridized BMW 5 Series sedans, Range Rover SUVs, and more. What's interesting here is that, for the most part, all of these cars were and are considered successes, with rare exceptions (Facel Vega Facellia, we're looking at you), which suggests luxury car buyers aren't actually all that hung up on the engine under the hood. Without further ado, here are our seven four-cylinder luxury cars, in chronological order.

Today, Fiat busies itself with budget-oriented and retro-themed compacts mainly, such as the seemingly evergreen 500, plus its new and immensely cute Panda Grande . Wind the clock back just over 120 years to 1905, though, and Fiat was a very different automaker. It was at this point that it debuted its 60 HP model to rival equivalent models from Mercedes. This thunderously powerful car was powered by a 647-cubic-inch inline-4 with dual-chain drive and a four-speed manual transmission. A 60-horsepower inline-4 might not sound like much at all by today's standards, but in vintage car circles, this Fiat is sometimes considered to be the original supercar.

The Fiat 60 HP had a split personality, designed to be capable both as a road-going vehicle and indeed as a racer, with removable wings and advanced cooling systems. It was also mightily expensive, commanding a $13,500 price tag in 1905, while the sole surviving example also wears a $4,000 coachbuilt touring body.

The craftsmen responsible for the body used only the finest materials available, including aluminum panels, silver solder to cover and hide fastening points, and brass mouldings to disguise the seams of the wooden framework. As for the interior, it was about as luxurious as one could expect for a car of this era, with leather seats and mohair floor mats. Remember, just owning a car in the early 20th century was a mind-boggling luxury, let alone one of this caliber.

There is much that could be said about the Facel Vega Facellia that is wholly negative, but for a car so imposing and bold in design, that seems unfair, so we shall begin with its stronger points. Facel Vega knew how to do style and opulence quite well, and although the Facellia was its entry-level model, this experience is still luxurious. It was poised as an excellent alternative to Mercedes' SL series, or indeed an equally charming Alfa Romeo of the same era. Inside, the expected amenities are all there in the form of leather seats and numerous gauges set into a hand-painted woodgrain-effect dashboard. On the outside, there is plenty of brightwork to enjoy, and the Facellia shares much in common stylistically with its bigger brother, the HK500.

However, what it sadly doesn't share with the HK500 is its hulking great Chrysler V8. Instead, the Facellia sported a notoriously unreliable French unit – a 115-hp 1.6-liter inline-4. It suffered from overheating issues, fragile internals, and troublesome chromed cylinder liners, which resulted in the majority of cars experiencing engine failure within the first six months of ownership. Facel Vega had no choice but to replace these engines free of charge, but those second engines didn't prove much better either. A final resolution came in the form of a genuinely bulletproof Volvo lump, but by this point, the firm's reputation was in the gutter, and the Facellia would ultimately prove a hurdle too high for the automaker.

This is a far more conventional offering than the other two covered so far. It replaced the aging P4 model in 1963, and production continued until 1977, so it was clearly a popular choice. With it, Rover successfully filled a notable gap in the UK's car market, where simple commuter cars generally sat at or below 1.5 liters in displacement, while large luxury models sported 3.0 liters or more. With its 2.0-liter inline-4, the P6 could jump between the two segments, offering a premium executive model that cost less than the larger luxury products.

“The stewards determined that the collision could have been avoided if the driver of car 81 had moved further to the left after Turn 1, even if this involved leaving the track prior to Turn 2.”

title: Can One Tire Really Do It All? 8 All-Weather Tires Compete To Find Out
raw_summary: Generally speaking, no one can have it all, and no one thing can do it all. That's just not how life works. And for the longest time, that was true of tires. You basically had to pick summer performance, winter performance, or disappointing so-called "all-seasons." Like with engines, though, tire technology advances, and the latest crop of all-weather tires claims to pretty much be able to do it all. But can a single tire really handle every single situation well? Our friends at Tyre Reviews compared eight of them to find out. The newest tire in the comparison is the Continental SecureContact AW, and when it comes to premium tires, a lot of times the newest one is the best. But is that the case here? Well, Tyre Reviews put it up against Michelin's legendary CrossClimate2, the Goodyear Assurance WeatherReady 2, Bridgestone's WeatherPeak, the Pirelli Cinturato WeatherActive, the Hankook Weatherflex GT, the Falken Aklimate, and the Atturo AZ810. And while this is supposedly a Continental-focused comparison, those of you who keep a sharp eye on Jalopnik's tire coverage will recognize that this is also an important comparison test for the much-improved Bridgestone WeatherPeak .
