This K-shaped economy has to be discouraging, but you need a car to live in America due to the lack of reliable public transportation, so you may as well be excited about it.

Sure, the world feels like it's collapsing around you, and you can barely afford to keep your head above water. And yes, enthusiast cars are typically even more expensive. Still, there are always alternative options that are underappreciated or even unloved that you can become excited about if you try. If the events you want to attend are too expensive, start your own. If the cars you like are too expensive, buy the cheaper version, a rough-condition example, or an undervalued competitor. If you can't be with the one you love, love the one you're with.

The great thing about car culture is that there's always a subculture for whatever car you're interested in. Whether you want to learn to drive better or you're more interested in engineering, whether you want more power or greater efficiency, or if you just want to make your car unique, there are groups of people out there for you to learn from. Be inquisitive, learn as much as you can, and develop your own flavor of car enthusiasm.

You don't know you're living in the good old days until they're already over. Across the last 20 years we've seen the near death of the affordable fun car. There was a time, not long ago, when every automaker offered three fun cars at any given time. The formative years of many Gen Z young adults saw the dissolution of convertibles, coupés, manual transmissions, and analog driving. What fun cars remained got more expensive, and electric cars brought pressure to note acceleration and lap time as the only measure of performance.
What fun cars will Gen Z collect once reaching their peak earning years? I predict it'll be the cars of their youth, split into three categories.

According to a recent Hagerty analysis of its insurance data, Gen Z car enthusiasts make up around 10% of insurance quote activity. That alone proves that the generation hasn't given up on enthusiast cars. Furthermore, the top five cars Hagerty says Gen Z shows outsized interest in are all pretty cool: Honda Beat, Acura RSX, Toyota Celsior, Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution VI, and Chevrolet Cobalt SS. With four of the five being Japanese imports, and most of them retailing in the mid-teens for a nice example, it kind of shows what their interests might be.

This list is a relatively affordable cross section of car culture in America. The Beat and RSX represent the sport compact car boom of Z youth. The Cobalt SS and Lancer Evo are legitimately good forced-induction punch-above-their-weight kinds of cars that just aren't made anymore. The Cobalt SS was the best-handling front-wheel drive car of its day, if not all time. The Celsior offers Mercedes-Benz-beating comfort and quality from the period for extremely little money. If you want one but don't want to deal with importing it, just buy a Lexus LS400 from the same period, and you'll have the same car with the steering wheel in the right place.

You're on the right page. These are all great places to start that won't break the bank. It takes some doing to find the right car for you and your budget, but there still are reasonably affordable options out there. Get the fun car while you're young.

I’ve joked here and on the Equity and Autonocast podcasts that the autonomous vehicle industry feels a lot like 2016, at least in terms of the buzziness surrounding the sector.
article_paragraphs: Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility , your hub for the future of transportation and now, more than ever, the role AI is playing in it. To get this in your inbox, sign up here for free — just click TechCrunch Mobility !
I’ve joked here and on the Equity and Autonocast podcasts that the autonomous vehicle industry feels a lot like 2016, at least in terms of the buzziness surrounding the sector.

But a recent conversation with Trucks VC partner Puneeth Meruva has me rethinking that comparison. There’s evidence that 2026 is even hotter — at least by certain measures — than those frothy dealmaking days of 2016 and 2017.

Trucks VC, which specializes in early-stage investing, has fielded pitches from 81 new autonomous vehicle startups so far in 2026 — two-thirds more than last year and enough to surpass the boom years of a decade ago. The VC firm argues in a new blog post that we’re in the midst of a second, even bigger AV wave fueled by technological breakthroughs. Yes, I’m talking about AI.

“For a long time AV companies were trying to go from what was AV 1.0 to AV 2.0, which is kind of this holy grail end-to-end architecture for AVs,” Meruva told me. “And I think the foundation models now provide a technical architecture that makes those end-to-end systems possible.”

These foundational models are particularly good at generalizing across different environments and scenarios, potentially making AVs cheaper and faster to deploy. The arrival of powerful open source models like Nvidia’s Alpamayo and Qwen’s general-purpose vision-language-action models has made it even easier for startups to get off the ground.

The barrier to entry is lower than ever before. Meruva said Trucks is consistently seeing startups deploy within a few months and with less than $1 million raised. (And while Meruva wouldn’t name names, the firm has invested in some of them.)

Of these 81 startups that pitched Trucks VC, I mistakenly assumed most would be applying their AV tech to construction, warehouse, agriculture, and mining. And yes, those were in the mix. But what surprised me was the growing number of startups pitching pure-play robotaxi businesses. And many are positioning themselves as direct competitors to Waymo.

raw_title: Westward Ho! First Trip Cross Country with Our New 2026 Tesla Model Y & Full Self Driving V14
title: Westward Ho! First Trip Cross Country with Our New 2026 Tesla Model Y & Full Self Driving V14
raw_summary: We were headed west again for the 6 th time, driving the ~1500 miles from our lake house in Northern Wisconsin to our winter home near the grandchildren in Northern Utah. We had totaled our 2019 Tesla Model 3 in an accident in May; therefore, this was our first road trip in our new 2026 Model Y running Full Self Driving V14. As usual, we were carrying two big ebikes on the back. We plan to pause in Utah at our home for a few days and then on to Portland, Oregon, and the Pacific Ocean. The experience was quite different this time because of the new car and the significant upgrade to Tesla’s driving automation: Full Self Driving Supervised V14.3.12.

We had totaled our 2019 Tesla Model 3 in an accident in May; therefore, this was our first road trip in our new 2026 Model Y running Full Self Driving V14. As usual, we were carrying two big ebikes on the back. We plan to pause in Utah at our home for a few days and then on to Portland, Oregon, and the Pacific Ocean.
The experience was quite different this time because of the new car and the significant upgrade to Tesla’s driving automation: Full Self Driving Supervised V14.3.12.

As we approached our first Supercharger in Wausau, Wisconsin, it looked like the navigation was taking us the wrong way. However, once we got to our normal exit, it was closed. We had to drive a few miles beyond it, do a U-turn, and come back. It cost us roughly an extra 5 miles. I’m going to have to learn to trust the navigation. The Nav knows about road closures like this and even traffic jams . Unfortunately, it doesn’t explain ahead of time why it is suggesting an alternate route.

Our first stop was at the Wausau, Wisconsin Supercharger next to the Hilton Gardens Inn on highway NN. In 7 years, we’ve never seen more than a few cars charging there. For the first time, the charging station was full (see photo below). It was Sunday after a big fall-colors week in Northern Wisconsin and many tourists were headed home. On our screen, it gave a charger wait time of five minutes. As we drove the last 100 miles to Wausau, our computer screen alternated between showing an unspecified wait time and as many as two stalls open.

When we arrived, it listed two stalls as open, but, in fact, for nearly the first time across the last seven years that we’ve been Supercharging, all eight stalls were full. However, here’s the good part: within less than five minutes, one of the cars pulled out and we were able to back into the empty stall . Then, the bad part: it was the slowest charge we’ve ever experienced. It was an older V2 hardware Supercharger where you need to share charging with the adjacent car. That meant that we were charging at only a 50-kilowatt speed for the whole charge. The total charge took about 40 minutes. However, after the bathroom break and walking our small rescue dog, Zuni, we only needed to kill about 15 minutes before setting off again.

The next stop was Menomonee, Wisconsin, halfway to Minneapolis and the charger was showing three empty stalls. Since, as I mentioned, we were traveling on a Sunday, a beautiful day, with full fall colors in the Northwoods, we found another Supercharger that appeared to be full (see below), but there was one stall empty and we pulled in. When we came east in mid-May, there were seldom more than one or two cars in any of the 12 Superchargers en route.

The Menomonee Supercharger has a newer Hardware 4 charger, so we were charging faster, at almost 100 kW during our whole charge. As we pulled out, there were about three cars waiting, but the line moved quickly. No one had to wait more than a few minutes. Then we were on our way to Minneapolis.

About 20 miles east of Minneapolis, crossing the Saint Croix River on the border between Wisconsin and Minnesota, half the lanes of the bridge were shut down. The navigation took us on a town of Henderson detour going on highways U and UU, then back onto the I-90 route across the bridge. It probably saved time avoiding the worst of the traffic backup because of the closure on the bridge. Then we were on an east–west route right through the center of Saint Paul–Minneapolis. Full Self Driving V14 with Tesla navigation found its way through the big city freeways perfectly.

raw_title: Bigger, badder Section 179 tax deduction could POWER UP fleet electrification [update]
title: Bigger, badder Section 179 tax deduction could POWER UP fleet electrification [update]
raw_summary: With national diesel prices inching towards $7/gallon and Tesla’s $290,000 Semi trucks finally making their way to paying customers , it’s worth revisiting how Trump’s One Big, Beautiful Bill Act (OBBA) helped beef up the Section 179 deduction, and look again at how it could help your fleet ditch diesel sooner rather than later. At the core of this thinking is the fact that the IRS does not distinguish between fuel choices, so there’s no separate depreciation category for electric- vs. diesel-fueled commercial trucks. The relevant classifications, then, are the vehicle’s use and property classes, and under the IRS’ depreciation guidelines, tractor units designed for over-the-road use are classified as 3-year properties and fall under the 20-year recovery threshold for 100% bonus depreciation, Tesla’s electric Semi can benefit from 179 just like their diesel-powered competitors. But don’t get me wrong – this isn’t just great news for Tesla Semi buyers. Electric garbage trucks , electric vocational trucks , battery electric reefer trailers , and even some big electric forklifts can potentially benefit from the same accelerated depreciation rules, since the IRS lists these as, “specialized business vehicles,” with no distinction between electric, diesel, natural gas, hydrogen , magic pixie dust, anything else.

There’s been some additional movement on the tax front since our original article, too. Earlier this year, the IRS issued Notice 2026-11, providing additional guidance on the permanent restoration of 100% bonus depreciation for qualifying property acquired after January 19, 2025 . That means that eligible businesses might be able to combine Section 179 expensing with bonus depreciation when ordering qualifying fleet equipment – and ordering is the key word. The IRS has specific rules for determining when equipment is considered acquired under a written, binding contract, and your tax professional and truck dealer can probably help you figure out a way to make those rules work in your favor.

You can check out the original article (with a few corrections sprinkled in to align with the latest guidance from Notice 2026-11 and Publication 946 ) below. Give it a read, read the disclaimer twice , then let us know what you think in the comments.

After the Commercial Clean Vehicle Credit (Section 45W) expired on September 30, the “experts” rushed out predictions of an EV sales slowdown in Q4. But, with over 6,800 pages in the Internal Revenue Code still in play, a turbocharged Section 179 tax deduction could still power a strong year for commercial EVs.

The One Big, Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) of 2025 gutted America’s energy independence goals and ensuring its auto industry would fall even further behind the Chinese in the EV race , but the loss of Section 45W wasn’t the only change written into the IRS’ rulebook. Section 179, an immediate expense reduction that business owners can take on depreciable equipment assets, has been made significantly more powerful for 2025.

The section 179 expense deduction is limited to such items as cars, office equipment, business machinery, and computers. This speedy deduction can provide substantial tax relief for business owners who are purchasing startup equipment.

The revised Section 179 tax credit (or, more accurately, expense reduction ) allows for a 100% deduction for equipment purchases has doubled to $2.5 million, with a phase-out kicking in at $4 million of capital investments that drops to zero at $6.5 million. That can be applied to new and used vehicles, as well as charging infrastructure, battery energy storage systems, specialized tools, and more (as long as they’re new to you).

title: What's The Difference Between A Plymouth Barracuda And A 'Cuda?
raw_summary: For the uninitiated, or those who just haven't given much thought to this end of the automotive spectrum, the '60s and '70s muscle car era is chock-full of extra-cool models, trims, engine choices, and more. It can also be incredibly confusing — based on which year, what was available with what, in which color, what particular option, and how do you decipher that through the VIN? On the Chrysler-Plymouth-Dodge Mopar front, there were quite a few combinations that have become immensely iconic. One of them being what one could find on the Plymouth Barracuda, but what's the difference between this epically cool nameplate and just a 'Cuda? In short, it's like Mopar's answer to the Pontiac Firebird Trans Am, or Chevy Camaro Z28; it was a more enthusiast-geared trim fitted with bodywork, colors, and engines to raise eyebrows (in a good way) and pulses. Let's dig into the badge's origin, when the 'Cuda came along, and what made it a cut above a standard Barracuda.

article_paragraphs: For the uninitiated, or those who just haven't given much thought to this end of the automotive spectrum, the '60s and '70s muscle car era is chock-full of extra-cool models, trims, engine choices, and more. It can also be incredibly confusing — based on which year, what was available with what, in which color, what particular option, and how do you decipher that through the VIN? On the Chrysler-Plymouth-Dodge Mopar front, there were quite a few combinations that have become immensely iconic. One of them being what one could find on the Plymouth Barracuda, but what's the difference between this epically cool nameplate and just a 'Cuda?

In short, it's like Mopar's answer to the Pontiac Firebird Trans Am, or Chevy Camaro Z28; it was a more enthusiast-geared trim fitted with bodywork, colors, and engines to raise eyebrows (in a good way) and pulses. Let's dig into the badge's origin, when the 'Cuda came along, and what made it a cut above a standard Barracuda.

The Barracuda nameplate itself debuted as a trim of the A-body-based Plymouth Valiant in 1964, featuring sportier bodywork and several engine choices: a 176-cubic-inch slant-six making 145 horsepower, the same cylinder configuration pumped up to 226 cubic inches and kicking out 170 horses, or the 180-horse, 273-cubic-inch V8. It was marketed as a smaller sporty two-door for the masses, and continued on until the generation ceased in 1966. It's important to point out that along the way in 1965, it became the Plymouth Barracuda, no longer marketed as the Plymouth Valiant Barracuda (which was too much to say, anyway). Fun fact: 1965 Plymouth Barracudas can be had for reasonable prices (like, less than $20,000) considering their vintage and prominence.

The second generation of the A-body car ran from '67 to '69 and came in three body styles: fastback, notchback, and convertible. This author's favorite is the fastback, thanks to its proportions. Chrysler's 383 cubic-inch V8 was available and made around 280 horsepower, and a very limited-production (i.e. now quite valuable) '68 Super Stock Barracuda with the legendary 426-cubic-inch Hemi V8 also debuted. Otherwise, the 318 was the standard V8 for 1968. A monstrous 440 Barracuda was also available.

The Barracuda truly was the enthusiast-geared trim in 1969, which is proven by its available engines: a 340, 383, and new-for-'68 440 cubic-inch V8. Then, the brand-new third-generation E-body Barracuda — available as either a coupe or a convertible — hit the market in '70. This is when the 'Cuda entered the high-performance limelight, and it got either a 340, 383, 426 Hemi, 440 Super Commando, or 440 Six-Barrel V8. The latter three had suspension upgrades and structural reinforcements to handle their high outputs, which were rated at 425, 375 and 390 hp, respectively. The plain ol' Barracuda just got either one of two sixes, the 318 V8, or the 383. That's it.

'71 was a particularly notable year, as it was the only 'Cuda to get gills (or, front fender louvers). Sadly, it was the last year of the 383, 440, and 426, too — the 340 was the top mechanical dog (displacement-wise) in '72, then the 360 in '73 and '74. The '70 and '71 Hemi 'Cuda is often referred to as the Holy Grail of the lineup as only 780 were sold. The generation then ended.

The difference between a Barracuda and a 'Cuda, then, comes down to available engines and enthusiast appeal — the gills of '71 definitely stick out the most, and there was a range of loud paint choices — like Lime Light green and Vitamin C orange — a shaker hood (which upped the drama from the driver seat view), and a Pistol Grip shifter on four-speed manual-equipped models. There's more to 'em, too, and they're definitely worth digging into and ogling further.

raw_title: This Microfiber Towel Mistake Could Ruin Your Ceramic Coating
title: This Microfiber Towel Mistake Could Ruin Your Ceramic Coating
raw_summary: Applying a ceramic coating can breathe new life into your car's paint . It helps the finish shimmer and provides hydrophobic properties, so water beads and rolls off almost instantly. However, if you're doing a ceramic coating yourself, it's wise to dispose of any microfiber towels after use. Ceramic coating products typically come with a small applicator pad, but if they don't, you can use a microfiber towel instead. Good quality towels with a density of around 250-350 GSM (grams per square meter) are recommended for removing excess coating before the curing process starts. If you're like me, you might hate throwing away microfiber towels. But if they come in contact with a ceramic coating that hasn't hardened yet, the coating will start crystallizing in the towel within minutes.
summary: Applying a ceramic coating can breathe new life into your car's paint . It helps the finish shimmer and provides hydrophobic properties, so water beads and rolls off almost instantly. However, if you're doing a ceramic coating yourself, it's wise to dispose of any microfiber towels after use.
article_paragraphs: Applying a ceramic coating can breathe new life into your car's paint . It helps the finish shimmer and provides hydrophobic properties, so water beads and rolls off almost instantly. However, if you're doing a ceramic coating yourself, it's wise to dispose of any microfiber towels after use.

Ceramic coating products typically come with a small applicator pad, but if they don't, you can use a microfiber towel instead. Good quality towels with a density of around 250-350 GSM (grams per square meter) are recommended for removing excess coating before the curing process starts. If you're like me, you might hate throwing away microfiber towels. But if they come in contact with a ceramic coating that hasn't hardened yet, the coating will start crystallizing in the towel within minutes.

These tiny crystals work their way deep into the towel's fibers, and if you use the towel on your car's paint in the future, you'll likely be left with scratches and swirl marks. Washing these towels isn't an option either. Proper ceramic coatings, like those sold by CarPro, Gtechniq, and Gyeon, are solvent-based, and not even warm water will break down the tiny nanoparticles, which often include silicon dioxide, titanium dioxide, and aluminum oxide.

A couple of years ago, I went through the arduous process of applying a ceramic coating to my car. I spent a full day carefully washing the car , and buffing and polishing the paint before applying Gyeon Pure Evo ceramic coating. It came out brilliantly and still sheds water just as well now as when it was fresh. I used several microfiber towels to buff and level the coating after the 'flashing' process, and ended up with a bunch of towels that lost their water-absorbing properties.

Although I could have thrown them out, I kept some for other cleaning tasks, but they'll never go anywhere near a car's paintwork again. For enthusiasts like us, a car's paint is often the first thing that catches our eye, and it's never nice to see light scratches that could have been prevented with a fresh set of towels rather than leftovers from a ceramic coating. Especially when detailing exotics like, say, a Koenigsegg Gemera.

The only time you might be able to re-use microfiber towels on your car's paint is if you used them with a spray-on 'ceramic' coating. Companies including Turtle Wax and Meguiar's sell spray coatings that promise easy, quick application. However, these spray-on ceramic products aren't true ceramic coatings as they don't have a high enough silicon dioxide content. In that case, you can get away with reusing microfiber towels from the application and buffing process, but it's wise to wash them thoroughly before any future use.

It helps the finish shimmer and provides hydrophobic properties, so water beads and rolls off almost instantly.

title: Cranberry Bogs Were Unprofitable, Then Solar Saved The Day
raw_summary: One of the things many people still don’t realize is how much solar power and wind power help farmers to be more profitable or to become profitable. Agriculture has never been the easiest industry, but it has been getting especially challenging to make ends meet in some parts of the world and with some types of farming. We now have news of a couple of cranberry bogs in Massachusetts that were out of service because of financial collapse but have now been saved by solar.

“ Distributed Energy Infrastructure (DEI) , a leading EPC provider for utility-scale solar and storage projects, announces the harvest of two groundbreaking cranberry agrivoltaics projects: the Black Cat Agrivoltaics Project in Plymouth, Massachusetts, and the Ring Road Agrivoltaics Project in Kingston, Massachusetts. Together, these projects have produced the first-ever agrivoltaic cranberry harvests — a milestone for expanding agrivoltaic applications into challenging wetland environments,” DEI shares .

“ The projects are owned by developer Greenbacker Renewables were installed by Distributed. Cranberry farmer Iain Ward, who manages the bogs, was closely involved throughout design and construction to ensure that the sensitive wetland environment remained intact. ”

“Building solar projects over active perennial wetland crops was an exciting challenge, and we’re thrilled to see the success of these harvests,” says Prateek Tare, Executive Vice President and Co-founder of DEI. “Iain’s collaboration and input at every stage was essential for us to ensure a reliable, cost-effective build while safeguarding the productivity of these heritage bogs.”

The Black Cat and Ring Road cranberry bogs had been out of service for years because they were no longer financially viable. However, the solar projects brought them back to life! “The solar projects now provide the landowner with additional income through land leasing, making the bogs’ cultivation economically viable again. Iain Warde is paid for agricultural management, in addition to his income from selling the cranberry crops.”

“Both projects were finalists for the North American Agrivoltaics Awards , and both Ward and DEI are founding members of the Solar & Farming Association (SAFA) . SAFA is a coalition of organizations representing the interests of the agrivoltaics industry, including developers, agricultural producers, livestock producers, and affiliated organizations.”
Agrivoltaics wins again. Farming and solar power is one of the best combos we’ve seen since someone decided to spread peanut butter and jelly together inside some slices of bread.

raw_title: What Is Your Dream Engine Swap?
title: What Is Your Dream Engine Swap?
raw_summary: Hang out in a group of car enthusiasts for long enough, and the topic will invariably turn toward bench racing. Whether you have the money, time, space, and mechanical ability to do so or not, you mentally build a neat car with cool details and offer it to the group for them to judge its coolness. Sometimes those dream builds make it out of the proverbial group chat, but often they don't. Whether you can commit to the build or not, or if it's just going to stay here, it's worth getting your idea out into the world. Maybe it'll inspire someone else here to get started on their own project, or even pivot their own idea because yours is cooler. For one reason or another, manufacturers don't always put their best engine in their best chassis, even though they probably could. Thankfully, there are backyard engineers and home mechanics everywhere capable of shoving whatever engine they want into a car, including engines that came from other manufacturers, or perhaps even engines never available in cars at all, like a high-revving motorcycle engine swap .

For one reason or another, manufacturers don't always put their best engine in their best chassis, even though they probably could. Thankfully, there are backyard engineers and home mechanics everywhere capable of shoving whatever engine they want into a car, including engines that came from other manufacturers, or perhaps even engines never available in cars at all, like a high-revving motorcycle engine swap .

Maybe your car didn't come with an engine that would make it perfect. I want to know all about it. What's your dream engine swap? Do you want to shove an LS into the back seat of a Geo Metro ? Do you want to put a Honda K-series into an old Datsun Roadster? Do you want to EV-swap your Lincoln Continental? Let's chat about it. Sound off in the comments below with your thoughts on engine and drivetrain swaps, and we'll discuss it. Then, I'll pick a few of my favorite responses to recap for everyone else next week.

I don't talk about it much, but the first fun car I ever bought was a 1976 Triumph TR-7 with a Buick 231 V6 under the hood. The swap wasn't done well, and the car was possessed with many demons. After acquiring it, I found out the car had significant rust damage, and the engine was much more worn out than I was promised. I pulled the engine and dedicated a winter of nights and weekends in college to rebuilding it. The car was eventually scrapped, but I still have that engine on a stand somewhere. I really should figure out what I'm going to do with it. That TR-7 was truly an abysmal car, and I probably should never have bought it, but it definitely helped shape my car enthusiasm and nurtured my love of engine swaps.

The car I've owned longest is my Porsche 912E (above), and it's been plagued with ignition issues for the last three years or so. I often think about pulling that original 2-liter flat four and replacing it with something that makes a bit more power and revs a bit higher. While a sane person would probably go buy a used flat-six from a later model 911, that's just too boring for my liking. Lately I've been thinking about building a Mazda 13B rotary engine to put in this little sucker. While the 912E was originally sold with about 88 horsepower, and a 2019 rebuild has it in the 110-hp range, I'd really like to see 150 or more for this little machine. A carbureted Formula Mazda 13B engine makes about 180 hp, and a modern Renesis makes just over 200. That should be plenty.

Think about how great a rotary would be in a Porsche chassis. It's still unorthodox enough that it pique the interest of at least a few people at a cars and coffee, but it's well-trodden enough territory that I wouldn't be walking into the wilderness. It's lighter, more powerful by a long shot, and it'll run out the tachometer to more than 4,500 rpm (and it'll sound good doing it). Maybe I'll start amassing the parts to get this project done over the winter. And maybe I'll talk about it more here in the near future.

raw_title: Bad Flock Info Leads Police To Tow Wrong Car, Then Towing Company Totals It
title: Bad Flock Info Leads Police To Tow Wrong Car, Then Towing Company Totals It
raw_summary: Police continue to blindly trust Flock cameras above and beyond the evidence in front of their own eyes. After incorrectly connecting Rosalyn Crump's car to a shooting that had occurred the previous day, police had her car towed and impounded as evidence, reports Moneywise . Within hours, they realized they had the wrong car. That doesn't magically reverse the damage the car suffered from being towed that led to it being declared totaled, leaving Crump without a car even though she did nothing wrong. Of course, a Flock camera was involved. In this case, it appears that it was not the technology that made a mistake, but the people using it. According to WWBT 12 On Your Side, Richmond, Virginia, police didn't have a license plate number for the suspect's car, making it impossible to search Flock's records for that plate. article_paragraphs: Police continue to blindly trust Flock cameras above and beyond the evidence in front of their own eyes. After incorrectly connecting Rosalyn Crump's car to a shooting that had occurred the previous day, police had her car towed and impounded as evidence, reports Moneywise . Within hours, they realized they had the wrong car. That doesn't magically reverse the damage the car suffered from being towed that led to it being declared totaled, leaving Crump without a car even though she did nothing wrong.

Of course, a Flock camera was involved. In this case, it appears that it was not the technology that made a mistake, but the people using it. According to WWBT 12 On Your Side, Richmond, Virginia, police didn't have a license plate number for the suspect's car, making it impossible to search Flock's records for that plate. Flock cameras collect more than just license plate information , so police searched for a make, model, color, and approximate model year.

Based on this extremely vague description, police zeroed in on Crump's 2012 Hyundai Elantra. Around 2 a.m. they started looking through the windows with flashlights to see what was in plain sight, which isn't technically a "search" — at least, not one that would require a warrant. Crump came outside to talk to police, who were absolutely certain her car was involved with the shooting. Body cam video obtained by 12 On Your Side shows her telling police:

This is the craziest thing I've ever seen in my life. ... I have had my car all day long. I was at my momma's house all day long. We came back here like 4 o'clock. I waited until my kids got off the bus at 5 o'clock.

Other body cam footage shows an officer expressing doubt that Crump's car is the right one, since child seats and other items inside seem inconsistent with a shooting. Another officer replies, "Don't be surprised if they would have set that up like that." Instead of believing the evidence, or Crump, or interviewing witnesses who could have corroborated her story, police called Seibert's Towing to impound the car.

Hours later, police identified a similar-looking car that seemed to be actually connected to the shooting, and released Crump's Elantra. Nobody actually told Crump this until four days later. Siebert's told Moneywise that police didn't actually release the car until then. Either way, they didn't tell her that Seibert's had ripped the front bumper off during the towing process — leaving the car undrivable — until she arrived to pick it up.

Seibert's took responsibility for causing the cosmetic damage, and was willing to cover the $2,212.30 bill to paint and replace the bumper cover, fog lights, and wheel liners. Then Crump asked for a full mechanical inspection, which revealed damaged tie rods and ball joints, jacking the bill beyond $6,000. Seibert's says it didn't cause this damage. Regardless of how it occurred, Siebert's insurer and Crump agree that her Hyundai is now a total loss due to the cost of the repairs it needs. It had been drivable, if mechanically worn, before police ordered it towed, damaging it for nothing more than a case of mistaken identity.

This is far from the first time we've seen police trusting Flock more than the evidence right in front of their eyes. In a similar situation in Lexington, Kentucky, heavily armed police surrounded a couple's home at 4 a.m. and questioned them about a road rage incident they had nothing to do with. The vehicle involved was a dark-colored Ram 2500, and theirs popped up on a Flock camera, with no evidence whatsoever linking it directly to the crime.

raw_summary: There’s been a lot of talk this year about a humongous AI bubble. We’ve written about that many times here on CleanTechnica , but focused on the US market. AI software companies have massive valuations/market caps based on hype and growth in AI use but without demonstrating anything close to profitability or a clear plan for profitability. That is not a typo.”

Of course, the robotics craze and the AI craze have been going hand in hand for the past year or two. This reporting seems to link the two.

raw_title: 11 Of The Most Powerful Pony Cars Ever To Leave The Factory
title: 11 Of The Most Powerful Pony Cars Ever To Leave The Factory
raw_summary: When Lee Iacocca set the pony car blueprint in 1964, the recipe was straightforward: compact footprint, modest mechanicals, and an affordable price tag. Over time, though, the pony car became more outrageous. Automakers started throwing big-block V8s in legends like the 1969 Mustang GT500 and 1970 Dodge Challenger R/T Hemi, blurring the line between the pony car and its bigger cousin, the muscle car. The Malaise Era and ever-stricter environmental laws toned down 1970s and 1980s pony cars, with 1990s models, like the 1998 Mustang SVT Cobra and the 1997 Camaro SS again reigniting the horsepower war. Still, it's the 21st century that gave us the most powerful pony cars to ever leave the factory, and it's not even close. From the 390-horsepower 2003 Ford SVT Mustang to the unhinged, 1,025-hp 2023 Challenger SRT, pony cars again dominated headlines.

From the 390-horsepower 2003 Ford SVT Mustang to the unhinged, 1,025-hp 2023 Challenger SRT, pony cars again dominated headlines.

Yes, we know, the Challenger's power figures, in particular, verge too much into muscle car, heck, even hypercar territory, but we'll let that pass, as it's a direct Mustang and Camaro competitor. We also love supercharged-V8 shenanigans here at Jalopnik, so every riotous version of Dodge's pony/muscle car, like the Super Stock and Demon 170, made the cut. With that settled, here are the 11 wildest pony cars to leave the factory floor!

Chevrolet let the Camaro bow down quietly after the 2024 model year, without any special, "last call" version. Not that this was strictly necessary — even in 2024, the ZL1 had more than enough oomph to satisfy seasoned Camaro enthusiasts. Packing the C7 Corvette Z06's 6.2-liter supercharged "LT4" V8 with 650 horsepower and 650 pound-feet of torque, the Camaro ZL1 catapults to 60 in 3.5 seconds. The 198-mph top speed is perhaps even more impressive, putting Chevy's pony car in the supercar league.

But the powertrain doesn't even scratch the surface of the Camaro ZL1's capability. This is a driver-oriented sports car, after all, with handling and poise atypical of pony cars. Part of the reason is the light, agile Alpha chassis, but also the suite of Nürburgring-tuned upgrades that turned Chevy's pony car into a legitimate corner carver. Most notably, the ZL1 features magnetic dampers, an electronically-controlled limited-slip differential, and Brembo calipers.

The 1LE package upped the ante with lightweight, aluminum Multimatic spool-valve dampers, rear aluminum bushings, smaller, lighter wheels, stickier tires, and adjustable front suspension geometry, allowing drivers to dial in aggressive negative camber for maximum track grip. As a cherry on top, the ZL1 was available with either a six-speed manual or a ten-speed auto, letting customers choose between higher performance and more engagement.

Armed with the 1LE package, the Camaro ZL1 morphed into a genuine supercar hunter, lapping the Nordschleife in 7:16.04 back in 2017. For reference, that made it faster around the legendary track than exotics like the Ferrari 488 (7:21.00), Lexus LFA (7:34.00), and Koenigsegg CCX (7:33.55).

Ford did the 600-plus horsepower, overpowered pony car a few years before its Chevy rival, but with a different approach. Instead of the Camaro ZL1's advanced independent rear suspension, the S197-II-generation Mustang Shelby GT500 used an antiquated live axle, which sounds scary on a car packing 662 horsepower and 631 pound-feet of torque.

article_paragraphs: Five years ago, I did something that seemed pretty ridiculous at the time. I bought a $2,000 electric mini-truck from China, had it shipped across the oceans to the US, and put it to work on my parents’ property in Florida.

The little white mini electric truck became something of an internet sensation, with my original unboxing and testing video quickly racking up over 10 million views, plus several million more from the follow-up videos.

It also attracted plenty of skeptics who were convinced that a $2,000 Chinese electric truck would fall apart within months, rust into oblivion, or otherwise prove to be a spectacular waste of money. “Good thing it has a bed,” was a common refrain. “So you can collect all the pieces that fall off along the way.”
I gave an update after the first year , showing that the truck was doing great. But to be fair, one year doesn’t tell us much.

Well now it’s been over five years, and I recently returned to Florida to see how the little truck has held up after five trips around the sun on my parents’ homestead. And I’ve got to say, the results are pretty surprising.
So here’s the truth about how the truck is doing five years later. Oh, and if you want to see it in action, you can check out my update video here . Trust me, you’ll want to.
First, it’s important to understand that this truck hasn’t spent five years sitting in a garage as some kind of novelty vehicle. It’s been a genuine workhorse on my parents’ 10-acre homestead.
Over the years, we’ve used it to haul everything from mulch and sand to lumber, tree branches, logs, yard waste, and everything in between.

title: Where Antonelli's 2026 will stand out among first-time F1 titles
raw_summary: Kimi Antonelli will become more than just Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion if, as looks near-certain, he clinches the 2026 title at the Mexican Grand Prix later today. The 20-year-old needs just two more points, equivalent to a single ninth place, from the remaining races to be champion, while remaining mathematical rivals George Russell and Lewis Hamilton effectively need to win all of the rest of this season’s races.

The 20-year-old needs just two more points, equivalent to a single ninth place, from the remaining races to be champion, while remaining mathematical rivals George Russell and Lewis Hamilton effectively need to win all of the rest of this season’s races.
article_paragraphs: Kimi Antonelli will become more than just Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion if, as looks near-certain, he clinches the 2026 title at the Mexican Grand Prix later today.

The 20-year-old needs just two more points, equivalent to a single ninth place, from the remaining races to be champion, while remaining mathematical rivals George Russell and Lewis Hamilton effectively need to win all of the rest of this season’s races.

He’ll be the 36th F1 world champion, but should be in a minority in that 20 of those clinched their first title in a final-race decider. Antonelli, by comparison, is cruising to the title and set to clinch it after 19 rounds. That will be with 82.6% of the season completed, by that metric the fifth-fastest of the first-time title-winners. He retains that position even if this season drops to 22 rounds, regardless of how you adjust the calculation.

Those ahead are led by Nigel Mansell, who finally won his only championship at the age of 39 in 1992 and sealed it with just 68.8% of the season gone. However, he was a veteran of title fights stretching back to 1986. Jim Clark (70% of the season in 1963) and Jackie Stewart (72.5% of the 1969 season) are next up.
The only other driver who won faster than Antonelli looks set to was Alberto Ascari (75% of the 1952 season) when the world championship was run for Formula 2 machinery.

Antonelli is poised to be one of only three drivers in the last 30 years who have sealed their first titles before the last round. That will put him in the illustrious company of Fernando Alonso (89.5% of the season in 2005) and Jenson Button (94.1% of the 2009 season).

All of these championships were won in different machinery against different levels of opposition, but Antonelli’s also stands out as something of a walkover. Even among the 16 first-time title wins that didn’t go down to the last round, some were genuine title fights that went deep into the season before swinging in one driver’s favour.

For example, Alain Prost’s 1985 championship for McLaren was sealed with two races to spare but Ferrari’s Michele Alboreto was right there with him before failing to score in the final five races. Alan Jones (1980), Button and Ayrton Senna (1988) and Alonso were all part of genuine battles.

title: Why Almost No Rental Car Company Will Let You Drive This Road In Alaska
raw_summary: In our species' relatively short time on it so far (in cosmic terms), we've already managed to pave around 40 million miles of roads. Still, not every bit of road is meant to be freely explored. One of those roads is Dalton Highway, a 414-mile road connecting central Alaska with the Prudhoe Bay oil fields, located in the far north and ending near the Arctic coastline. If you're a "Game of Thrones" fan and imagine this to be likened to the lands North of the Wall, well, you'd be quite right. It's beautiful, and there is some incredible scenery along the way, but many perils await. Not White Walkers, but other hazards make this one of the most dangerous roads in the world .

article_paragraphs: In our species' relatively short time on it so far (in cosmic terms), we've already managed to pave around 40 million miles of roads. Still, not every bit of road is meant to be freely explored.

One of those roads is Dalton Highway, a 414-mile road connecting central Alaska with the Prudhoe Bay oil fields, located in the far north and ending near the Arctic coastline. If you're a "Game of Thrones" fan and imagine this to be likened to the lands North of the Wall, well, you'd be quite right. It's beautiful, and there is some incredible scenery along the way, but many perils await. Not White Walkers, but other hazards make this one of the most dangerous roads in the world .

There are no service stations for a seemingly endless portion, and very few spots where you'll get cell phone signal. The road conditions are largely unpaved, and you'll need to be wary of huge semi-trucks, since the route is mostly for commercial transport. Given the sheer length of the highway, there's a chance you may encounter large wildlife, some of which can look at you as dinner.

Put these problems together, and it becomes clear why, even according to the Alaska Department of Transportation's website , many car rental companies either refuse to pay for any vehicle damage sustained on the road, or outright won't loan you a car if you say you're going there. However, you can still find a few rental companies that permit driving on unpaved roads, like the Dalton Highway, such as Alaska 4x4 Rentals .

Dalton Highway has a roughly 240-mile stretch with no service stations at all , which, to give you some perspective, is almost the driving distance between Dallas and Houston (269 miles). This is considered by many to be the longest gap between two gas stations in the entirety of North America, so as you can imagine, it's imperative that you're well-stocked with extra supplies for both yourself and your car.

Because the highway's surface is mostly dirt and gravel as opposed to pavement, don't expect the journey to be smooth sailing. During the winter – which can start as early as August and stretch into June, or even July — there's the added complication of snow and ice. Avalanches have stranded travelers for days at a time, and with temperatures dropping as low as minus 80 degrees Fahrenheit, even the best winter drivers have their work cut out .

There's naturally a higher chance of breakdown considering how much your car is going through on this highway. "No biggie, I'll just call a towing service, catch something to eat, and enjoy the epic scenery," you may be thinking. It isn't quite that simple.

Dalton Highway has expanded its cell phone service in recent years. Still, most of the stretch doesn't offer a signal, making a CB radio a solid backup. If you break down, you can get a tow truck to pick you up, but it'll likely be very expensive. Dalton Highway Towing, for example, charges a base fee of $200 for the first half-hour (plus mileage fees), and then a subsequent $75 for every half-hour beyond that. Apparently, some drivers have had to wait over 24 hours for their knight in shining armor to arrive, so do take this into consideration.

raw_title: How Much Would It Cost To Buy A New Corvette In 2007 Vs. 2027?
title: How Much Would It Cost To Buy A New Corvette In 2007 Vs. 2027?
raw_summary: It's fun to look back at old magazines, movies, TV shows and commercials, and laugh — or cry — at how cheap cars and gas were in years gone by. But did yesterday's gearheads really get a better deal, or is it simply inflation tricking us into thinking they did? Was a Corvette more affordable in real terms in 2007, for example, than a 2027 model is today? We dug through old price lists and discovered that, while the 2007 C6 Vette initially appears to be almost half the price of a new C8, the pair cost near identical amounts when inflation is taken into account. The sixth-generation C6 Corvette debuted at the Detroit Auto Show in January 2004, and went into production that summer as a 2005 model, in coupe and convertible form. Both came with a new 6.0L LS2 V8 that made 400 horsepower. But buyers got an even hotter option for 2006 with the return of the high-performance Z06 , this time with a naturally aspirated 7.0L LS7 V8 and 505 hp. The base Corvette had two body style choices and the option of automatic or manual transmissions, but the C6 Z06 was only ever offered as a manual coupe.

The base Corvette had two body style choices and the option of automatic or manual transmissions, but the C6 Z06 was only ever offered as a manual coupe.

Period documents tell us the base 2007 Corvette coupe cost $44,995 (including $825 destination) in the fall of 2006, which is about $73,120, adjusted for inflation to current values using pricing data from the U.S. Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics. The 2007 convertible cost $52,910 ($85,980 adjusted), and replacing the standard six-speed manual transmission with the available six-speed automatic, added $1,250 ($2,030).

The higher performance Z06 required a more serious financial commitment. It stickered at $70,000 ($113,750 adjusted). But how do those prices compare with what your Chevy dealer wants for the 2027 Corvette?

Fast forward to 2027 and the Corvette is a very different machine. The C8 Vette ushered in a mid-engined design, and although the initial 2020 lineup was limited to the basic Stingray, six years on there are six different Corvettes, with five distinct powertrains. But today's Corvette range still has a base coupe and convertible, and a Z06, so we can directly compare 2007 and 2027 prices.

Remember how we said the base C6 coupe would be $73,120 in today's money? Its modern equivalent is incredibly close on price, coming in at $73,795 (including $2,495 destination), and that includes a standard eight-speed dual-clutch automatic. Going for the roadster results in a $80,795 bill, which makes it $5,185 cheaper than the inflation-adjusted 2007 Corvette convertible. The Stingray, and new $88,795 Grand Sport that out-grips the Z06 , also get a fresh 6.7L V8 engine for 2027, making 535 hp.

But the Z06 has definitely grown in price. The C8 Corvette Z06 has a naturally aspirated 5.5L V8 that sends 670 hp to the rear wheels, and it costs $121,695 in basic 1LZ spec, or $7,945 more than the C6 Z06, adjusted to present-day values. The availability of a convertible Z06 (for $128,695) is another big shift between the generations.

Think that sounds expensive? There are plenty of opportunities to spend even more on a new C8 Corvette. The ZR1 adds twin turbochargers to the Z06's flat-plane crank V8, giving you 1,064 hp for $197,495 as a coupe, or $207,495 as a convertible. And the quarter-mile-crushing ZR1X , an all-wheel drive Corvette with two front electric motors that boost total output to 1,250 hp, starts at $227,695. Which is about $200,000 more than a nice used C6.

title: The Amphibious Fat Truck - A 4×4 And Boat In One
raw_summary: This is a Fat Truck from Canadian company Zeal Motor, each is four-wheel-drive and can operate as a boat on water, or as a highly-capable ATV on land. Interestingly, Zeal notes that only the wheels come from outside North America. 60% of the parts come from the USA, including the turbodiesel engine, and the rest of the parts come from within 300 miles of the Canadian factory.

Interestingly, Zeal notes that only the wheels come from outside North America. 60% of the parts come from the USA, including the turbodiesel engine, and the rest of the parts come from within 300 miles of the Canadian factory.

Zeal Motor unveiled the new Fat Truck amphibious vehicle in Bromont, Quebec, in January of 2019, with a 40 bhp three-cylinder diesel in its hull. Zeal quickly decided to replace that original 1.7 liter Caterpillar unit with a more powerful 2.2 liter Caterpillar four-cylinder turbodiesel capable of a healthier 67 bhp and 153 lb ft of torque.
Above Video: This clip from Caterpillar shows the Zeal Motor Fat Truck being put through its paces, on land and on the water.

In short, the Fat Truck is an amphibious crew and cargo carrier for work sites that a conventional 4×4 can’t reach. Common use cases include power line and pipeline work, telecom tower maintenance, wind farm upkeep, and search-and-rescue operations in remote backcountry. Unusually, it has no steering wheel and no pedals, instead it changes direction using a tank-like skid-steering system.

Zeal’s three founders were Maxim O’Shaughnessy, Benoit Marleau, and Amine Khimjee. They each come from a background in industrial vehicles, with 60 years of combined experience that included time at the crawler carrier manufacturer Prinoth.

While looking for a product for clients with extreme off-road transport needs, they tested the Ukrainian-built Sherp , a big-wheeled amphibious ATV. O’Shaughnessy’s idea was to combine those oversize wheels with the core features of an industrial machine. The partners found the Sherp effective, but they also found it difficult to drive, and its cabin could quickly fill with fumes.

Development began in May of 2018, Zeal had set up its headquarters in part of the former Hyundai plant in Bromont, and 2,000 hours of engineering work had already been done under Marleau, the vice president of engineering. Industrial designer Martin Aubé developed the body – a tall box with no overhangs to speak of, roughly as wide as it is high, with large tinted windows on all four sides.

raw_title: Why It's Hard To Pin Down What Kinds Of Cars Actually Qualify As 'Exotics'
title: Why It's Hard To Pin Down What Kinds Of Cars Actually Qualify As 'Exotics
raw_summary: Humans love to label and categorize everything because it helps us make sense of the world. Cars are no exception. In many people's eyes, the Porsche 911 Turbo S, for example, is a sports car, not a supercar, and the same goes for the Corvette C8 Z06. Meanwhile, the Ferrari F430 and McLaren 570S are supercars, and the McLaren F1 is a hypercar. Yet looking at the actual numbers, the 911 and the ZR1 are both quicker than the aforementioned supercar and hypercar, which makes no sense. The Lamborghini Miura is often credited as the car that popularized the term "supercar," but the word itself existed long before the Miura . So, even pinning down the first supercar is a mess, which tells you everything about how these labels work. And that's exactly why nailing down what qualifies as exotic is just as messy.
summary: Humans love to label and categorize everything because it helps us make sense of the world. In many people's eyes, the Porsche 911 Turbo S, for example, is a sports car, not a supercar, and the same goes for the Corvette C8 Z06. Meanwhile, the Ferrari F430 and McLaren 570S are supercars, and the McLaren F1 is a hypercar.
article_paragraphs: Humans love to label and categorize everything because it helps us make sense of the world. Cars are no exception. In many people's eyes, the Porsche 911 Turbo S, for example, is a sports car, not a supercar, and the same goes for the Corvette C8 Z06. Meanwhile, the Ferrari F430 and McLaren 570S are supercars, and the McLaren F1 is a hypercar. Yet looking at the actual numbers, the 911 and the ZR1 are both quicker than the aforementioned supercar and hypercar, which makes no sense.

The Lamborghini Miura is often credited as the car that popularized the term "supercar," but the word itself existed long before the Miura . So, even pinning down the first supercar is a mess, which tells you everything about how these labels work. And that's exactly why nailing down what qualifies as exotic is just as messy.

There are no strict definitions, because this isn't science — it's pop culture. A car becomes exotic once enough people who shape the conversation decide it is. The answer is also different depending on whom you ask. Some tie the label to a car's rarity, performance, and how loaded it is with luxury touches, while others say a car can earn the label through small production runs, hand-built construction, or a tie to a meaningful moment in automotive history.

Materials and shape matter too – heavy use of exclusive materials such as carbon fiber and titanium, wrapped in a body that sits low and narrow, only add to the case. Hagerty , meanwhile, treats the term "exotic" as an insurance-industry catch-all rather than a strict definition — one wide enough to cover everything from an entry-level luxury sports car like the BMW M6 to a full-blown hypercar like the McLaren Senna.

As an example, take the Porsche 911 Turbo S. Plenty of people call it just a very fast sports car, not an exotic – Car and Driver even called it "supercar-adjacent." Others argue its performance alone earns it the title. The Corvette C8 Z06 gets the same treatment from the other side. Some see it as America's answer to a European supercar. Others can't get past the fact that it's still a Corvette. Even the people who define these categories for a living can't seem to agree. Take Timothy Burton, better known as Shmee150 — while driving the range-topping, 1,250-horsepower ZR1X alongside a convoy of C8s, he asked out loud on camera, "Are we a sports car?" before settling on "sports car with hypercar performance" as the only way to describe it.

In his YouTube video aptly titled "Exotic Cars You're Wrong About," Doug DeMuro pointed out that Acura built fewer than 3,000 units of the second-generation NSX, calling it "a smaller production run than the Ford GT, which is a car that everybody thinks is such an iconic, special, amazing vehicle." By that logic, the NSX is rarer. Yet the NSX's exotic status is up for debate, while the Ford GT's mostly isn't.

Enthusiasts are also divided. In a FerrariChat debate about the V10 Audi R8, one person argued that mass carmakers couldn't build exotics; others pointed to the Ford GT as a counterexample. A Reddit discussion even split over the Porsche 918, with one commenter excluding every Porsche and another insisting the 918 qualified. These arguments suggest the disagreement never ends. Some judge the individual car's merits; others give more weight to the badge.

To help us understand what an exotic car might be, we can also try to look at it from a different direction — by telling you what it isn't. For starters, an exotic car is clearly not your run-of-the-mill economy car like the Nissan Altima, Honda Odyssey, or RAV4. These cars are built in massive numbers, are always accessible, offer adequate performance for daily driving, and most importantly, they don't try to be exotic in any way.

raw_title: Here's How Much 2022 Volkswagen Taos Models Have Depreciated In 4 Years
title: Here's How Much 2022 Volkswagen Taos Models Have Depreciated In 4 Years
raw_summary: Volkswagen boasts a fairly comprehensive lineup of SUVs that began way back in 2002 with the release of the Touareg. Over the years, models such as the Tiguan and Atlas have joined the fold, followed more recently by the Taos for the 2022 model year. Offered as an affordable entry point into the world of German SUV ownership, the Taos is a two-row subcompact model. It debuted with a sticker price of $24,190, including a $1,195 destination fee. Fast-forward to today, and a 2027 Taos commands $28,025 with destination.
summary: Volkswagen boasts a fairly comprehensive lineup of SUVs that began way back in 2002 with the release of the Touareg. Over the years, models such as the Tiguan and Atlas have joined the fold, followed more recently by the Taos for the 2022 model year.
article_paragraphs: Volkswagen boasts a fairly comprehensive lineup of SUVs that began way back in 2002 with the release of the Touareg. Over the years, models such as the Tiguan and Atlas have joined the fold, followed more recently by the Taos for the 2022 model year.

Offered as an affordable entry point into the world of German SUV ownership, the Taos is a two-row subcompact model. It debuted with a sticker price of $24,190, including a $1,195 destination fee. Fast-forward to today, and a 2027 Taos commands $28,025 with destination.

Thankfully, used shoppers can net themselves an impressive saving by opting for a 2022 Taos, which, according to Kelley Blue Book (KBB), is available at a huge discount now that a few years have passed. The site advises a Fair Purchase Price that kicks off from just $15,950, or $14,650 as a Private Party Value, so up to $9,540 less than its original sticker price.

That's an impressive chunk to have lost in just four model years, but that's only on the base trim. It's also important to explore the full picture across the Taos's entire range of grades, which includes both front- and all-wheel-drive variants of S, SE, and SEL trims. But depreciation works in mysterious ways , so we'll also explore why the Taos drops as much value as it does, and how it compares to other SUVs within its segment.

A quick look at KBB reveals that current values do still align with what they cost new, in that the more expensive trims — like the SEL and SEL 4MOTION grades — command higher prices today. Those trims cost $32,685 and $34,240, respectively, when new, and today, KBB advises Fair Purchase Prices of $18,150 and $18,500. That's certainly more than lesser trims such as the $15,950 S, but in dollar terms, those who spent more on higher trims have lost more.

While Fair Purchase Prices show the S has shed $8,240 in value, the SEL 4MOTION has shed $15,740 over the same period — a bitter pill to swallow. KBB bases its estimates on national averages typical for the model, but admits real-world results can vary, depending on numerous external factors.

With that in mind, live listings offer a useful real-world check. Filtering AutoTempest listings for clean titles and average mileage, we found that KBB's estimates aren't far from the truth. There are only a handful of base S models to be found south of $15,000, while SE models become more common between $16,000 and $17,000. As for SEL models, $18,500 does seem accurate, although plenty are still asking around $20,000, so the KBB figures shouldn't be seen as a strict rule.

Losing around $10,000 or more to depreciation in just four model years might seem reasonable on, say, a car that costs over $50,000, but on a $25,000 Taos, that's a significant portion of the car's value to shed. It might give prospective buyers of a new Taos food for thought.

raw_summary: Yamaha has informed MotoGP it will not take part in the 2026 Qatar Grand Prix next weekend, citing "company-wide travel restrictions", and now faces penalties from the championship. The manufacturer has issued a press release revealing it communicated to the series that it does not plan to run its four bikes in the upcoming race weekend at the Lusail track, amid conflict in the region and fears of an escalation in the ongoing USA-Iran war.

article_paragraphs: Yamaha has informed MotoGP it will not take part in the 2026 Qatar Grand Prix next weekend, citing "company-wide travel restrictions", and now faces penalties from the championship.

The manufacturer has issued a press release revealing it communicated to the series that it does not plan to run its four bikes in the upcoming race weekend at the Lusail track, amid conflict in the region and fears of an escalation in the ongoing USA-Iran war.
"Following its latest assessment of the situation in the Middle East, Yamaha has not identified sufficient grounds to change its existing company-wide travel restrictions," the statement read.
"As a result, Yamaha has informed MotoGP Group about its decision not to participate in the 2026 Qatar Grand Prix.
"This decision reflects Yamaha’s assessment of the information currently available and is independent of the measures implemented by MotoGP Group and the event organizer.
"Yamaha remains fully committed to MotoGP and looks forward to returning to competition at the Portuguese Grand Prix."
MotoGP responded with a statement saying it felt it had given the paddock adequate reassurances over Qatar, and that Yamaha was now in line for penalties for breaking its contractual commitments.
"MotoGP is disappointed by Yamaha's decision not to participate in the Qatar Grand Prix," it read.

title: F1's attempt to prevent a repeat of Mexico Turn 1 antics
raw_summary: Formula 1’s Mexican Grand Prix stewards have issued a statement to all teams and drivers to try to avoid a repeat of the opening lap shenanigans of last year’s race. Lando Norris, Max Verstappen and the Ferraris of Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton went four-wide into Turn 1 on the first lap in 2025, with both Verstappen and Leclerc cutting across the grass.
summary: Formula 1’s Mexican Grand Prix stewards have issued a statement to all teams and drivers to try to avoid a repeat of the opening lap shenanigans of last year’s race. Lando Norris, Max Verstappen and the Ferraris of Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton went four-wide into Turn 1 on the first lap in 2025, with both Verstappen and Leclerc cutting across the grass.
article_paragraphs: Formula 1’s Mexican Grand Prix stewards have issued a statement to all teams and drivers to try to avoid a repeat of the opening lap shenanigans of last year’s race.
Lando Norris, Max Verstappen and the Ferraris of Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton went four-wide into Turn 1 on the first lap in 2025, with both Verstappen and Leclerc cutting across the grass.
Leclerc initially emerged comfortably in the lead but lifted off into the Turn 4 left-hander and allowed Norris ahead.
In fact, a fifth of the grid cut the track at Turn 1 - as Kimi Antonelli, Carlos Sainz and Liam Lawson also took the grass route.

This left George Russell, who had a front-row seat behind the top four on lap one, furious after the race as he said: “I just struggle to understand how three guys can just cut the corner and maintain their position. They got it wrong, they brake too late, they made a mistake.
“But then they can just cut the corner and continue, and there was no punishment for their mistake.

“So I was pretty pissed off with that to start with and then, when Max went off the track at Turn 4, came back on, and it was wrong place, wrong time for me but, again, that should’ve been penalised as well.”
Russell will be pleased to know the stewards have proactively issued clarification of how the driving standard guidelines will be applied on the first lap in Mexico this year.

raw_title: How Ocon's replacement is really faring on his shock F1 debut
title: How Ocon's replacement is really faring on his shock F1 debut
raw_summary: Ryo Hirakawa was about to go for his usual run on Saturday morning in Mexico when he got the call telling him he would get the opportunity "I've always been ready for" to qualify for his Formula 1 debut. Despite the short notice, Haas’s shock Esteban Ocon replacement was disappointed not to reach Q2 in 19th place given his final qualifying run was compromised by traffic.
summary: Ryo Hirakawa was about to go for his usual run on Saturday morning in Mexico when he got the call telling him he would get the opportunity "I've always been ready for" to qualify for his Formula 1 debut. Despite the short notice, Haas’s shock Esteban Ocon replacement was disappointed not to reach Q2 in 19th place given his final qualifying run was compromised by traffic.
article_paragraphs: Ryo Hirakawa was about to go for his usual run on Saturday morning in Mexico when he got the call telling him he would get the opportunity "I've always been ready for" to qualify for his Formula 1 debut.
Despite the short notice, Haas’s shock Esteban Ocon replacement was disappointed not to reach Q2 in 19th place given his final qualifying run was compromised by traffic.

The 32-year-old long-time Toyota driver, a Le Mans 24 Hours winner and two-time World Endurance champion, received unusually late notice that he would take over Ocon's car for the remainder of the weekend.

Hirakawa wasn't driving it cold having run in FP1, his ninth outing since late-2024 in F1 sessions, and having also logged a combined total of 4541km (2822 miles) in the 2023 and '25 Haas cars over the past two years. But even so he was in at the deep end.

FP3 was inevitably a compressed, intensive session in which no driver logged more laps than he did. The work was efficient, with clear communication to and from race engineer Laura Mueller as they crammed in a mini-long run, practice starts, qualifying simulations and took multiple opportunities to refine how he attacks the pit box. That included one practice pitstop without a tyre change that let him also hone the release. It meant he went into qualifying relatively confident, even if he recognised there was plenty he needed to tidy up.

Both Haas drivers completed three runs in Q1, with Hirakawa 0.330 seconds slower than team regular Ollie Bearman on the first lap - a deliberately neat and tidy banker effort - then 0.304s slower on the second as both made a similar step. The main deficit was in the final sector comprising the stadium section and last corner where, as Hirakawa pointed out, "as soon as you slide you [pay] the price]".

Hirakawa failed to improve on his final attempt and ended up 0.875s down in 19th while his team-mate advanced to Q2. However, that was not down to him not having the edge when it came to extracting the peak of grip at the end of the session.

He improved on his personal best time in sectors one and three, but had Alex Albon ahead in the middle sector. Albon wasn't directly impeding him, but he created costly aerodynamic turbulence and left Hirakawa disappointed. The time loss started with a little given away through Turn 4-6 at the start of the second sector, which he started 4.5s behind Albon, and got worse in the esses.

Though he finished on the podium this Sunday at Sepang, one of his best tracks in MotoGP, Marquez has felt limited by continued management of a right shoulder injury he sustained in his brutal crash during the Catalan Grand Prix in May.
"From the moment that I came back after the Catalunya accident, I suffered a lot with my right shoulder," he said.

article_paragraphs: Honda has spent decades building one of the most dominant positions in the global motorcycle industry, selling millions of gasoline-powered two-wheelers each year. But in markets where electric motorcycles and scooters are becoming increasingly accessible, that dominance is starting to face a serious challenge.
Vietnam offers a particularly interesting case study, where rapidly growing electric motorcycle sales are beginning to reshape a market long dominated by Honda.

According to newly released nationwide sales figures , Vietnam saw more than 3 million motorcycle and scooter sales during the first nine months of 2026, representing 25.9% growth over the same period last year.

But the real story is in the electric segment, where sales surged 90.5% to reach 973,247 units. That means electric two-wheelers now account for approximately 32% of all new motorcycle and scooter sales in the country.
And the biggest beneficiary isn’t Honda. It’s actually Vietnamese electric vehicle manufacturer VinFast.

While Honda remains Vietnam’s largest motorcycle manufacturer overall, with sales growing 8.4% this year, VinFast has surged into second place with a staggering 152.1% increase in sales. Yamaha now sits in third place, followed by electric two-wheeler manufacturer Yadea in fourth.
Of the top four players, half are electric, and it’s precisely that half that is experiencing meteoric sales growth.
It’s an impressive reshuffling of a market that has traditionally been dominated by Japanese gasoline motorcycle manufacturers.

Marquez overtook polesitting brother Alex into Turn 1, then rebuffed a counter-attack at Turn 4 as Alex couldn't quite get his Gresini Ducati stopped to complete the move.

They ran in tandem for the next few laps, with a charging Pedro Acosta moving up to third after a feisty opening lap - but Alex simply had no answer for Marc's pace further into the race, as the gap between the two tipped over a second on lap seven of 20.
By the time Acosta worked his way past Alex Marquez with a move into the hard braking zone of Turn 9, Marc was already nearly two seconds clear.
And the change in second place made little difference to his race, as the elder Marquez ultimately won by a commanding 4.1s - the third-highest grand prix winning margin of the season.
With Acosta and Alex Marquez joining him on the podium, there was further disillusionment for Aprilia late on as Marco Bezzecchi's grand prix fell apart.

Bezzecchi had overtaken Aprilia stablemate Ai Ogura early on, and looked like joining the podium battle - but never quite did, instead falling into the clutches of the Japanese rider in the closing laps.

title: Australian Icon: A 1963 Holden EH “Special”
raw_summary: This is a 1963 Holden EH Special, it’s an Australian sedan that dominated the southern nation’s sales charts back in the 1960s, and remained a common sight on roads until well into the 1980s. This car is an EH Special, denoting the fact that it was a more upmarket version of the model, a special-equipment example with more chrome and better trim.
article_paragraphs: This is a 1963 Holden EH Special, it’s an Australian sedan that dominated the southern nation’s sales charts back in the 1960s, and remained a common sight on roads until well into the 1980s.

This car is an EH Special, denoting the fact that it was a more upmarket version of the model, a special-equipment example with more chrome and better trim. This car had the largest engine on offer, the 179 cubic inch (2.9 liter) straight-six affectionately known as the Holden Red motor.

Holden released their new EH model in August of 1963, they would ultimately sell over a quarter of a million of them over three model years, 256,959 in total , and it soon became one of the most common family cars on Australian roads. The body of the EH was closely based on the earlier Holden EJ model, and Holden later described the EH as the fastest-selling Australian car ever.

Holden released their new EH model in August of 1963, they would ultimately sell over a quarter of a million of them over three model years, 256,959 in total, and it soon became one of the most common family cars on Australian roads. Image courtesy of General Motors Holden.

The Holden EJ sedan of mid-1962 had been the first all-new Holden of the decade, it was lower and sleeker than the outgoing EK it replaced and introduced the Premier variant, Holden’s first ever luxury model, but it kept the old suspension and the 138 cubic inch (2.3 liter) “Grey” straight-six with a measly 75 bhp. Holden built 154,811 EJs in 13 months, it sold well, but it was clear that a new model was needed to stay competitive with their arch rivals over at Australia’s Ford operations.

The new EH sedan changed far more of that body than Holden’s earlier facelifts had. The roof, rear quarters, trunk, front fenders, hood, grille and tail lights were all brand new, giving a squarer profile, though the ute and panel van kept the older EJ tail lights. The Standard EH sedan remained at the EJ’s price, but it offered a lot more car for the money.

The new straight-six took its nickname from the bright red color of its block . It was a fresh design rather than a development of the earlier Grey six, a pushrod overhead-valve unit with seven main bearings and a single-barrel Bendix-Stromberg carburetor, built in two sizes on a common 3.00 inch stroke. The 149 cubic inch (2.4 liter) version made 100 bhp at 4,400 rpm and 145 lb ft of torque at 2,000 rpm, with a 95 bhp low-compression alternative.

Opening the bore from 3.25 to 3.563 inches gave the 179 cubic inch (2.9 liter) engine 115 bhp at 4,000 rpm and 175 lb ft of torque at 1,600 rpm, 53% more power than the Grey with a much stronger bottom end to boot.

raw_title: Why The Toyota Hilux Is One Of The Most Legendary Compact Trucks Ever Built
title: Why The Toyota Hilux Is One Of The Most Legendary Compact Trucks Ever Built
raw_summary: You'd probably agree that there aren't many brands with a reputation for building long-lasting cars like Toyota's . And within the Japanese automaker's lineup sits a pickup truck that, although fairly unpopular stateside, enjoys legendary status elsewhere around the globe: the Toyota Hilux. It's almost impossible to talk about the Hilux and not mention Top Gear's elaborate little excursion, which played quite a significant role in lending the compact truck its "indestructible" title. Even after subjecting it to many grueling events, including setting it on fire and drowning it in seawater, the Hilux simply refused to die, only needing a few basic tools and a bit of mechanical sympathy to get it running again. You may have also seen James May drive one up an active volcano, which was the same Hilux the camera crew used while filming the Polar Special, where he accompanied Jeremy Clarkson in their expedition to the North Pole — also in a Hilux.
